summary: Survey MCOS for UEFI boot hardening, OOBE logic bugs, offline Fabric bundling, and framebuffer UI groundwork

surveys.summary: The EFISTUB fallback is fully gone from the current installer — no path anywhere in the repo copies a raw kernel to BOOTX64.EFI, no startup.nsh is written, and every boot path goes through GRUB with an explicit `linux` command line; both GRUB prefixes (UEFI `/EFI/BOOT`, BIOS `(hd0,msdos1)/boot/grub`) match where mcos-install actually writes grub.cfg, and I verified the BIOS dd mechanics byte-for-byte (boot.img kernel_sector=1, core.img blocklist start=2/len=321). Resolution is controlled solely by `set gfxmode` in grub.cfg plus `gfxpayload=keep`; the kernel enables no native KMS driver (no i915/amdgpu/radeon/nouveau), so on bare metal the mode comes from the bootloader and cannot be changed at runtime — and none of the three test scripts would catch either a kernel-at-BOOTX64.EFI regression or a grub.cfg/prefix mismatch.

facts.claim: The EFISTUB fallback is completely gone from the current working-tree installer. It existed at git HEAD and was removed.
facts.evidence: `git show HEAD:.../mcos-install | grep -i EFISTUB` returns lines 138-141: `if [ ! -f /mnt/target/boot/EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI ] && [ -f /mnt/target/boot/bzImage ]; then` / `log "EFISTUB fallback (Kernel EFI STUB) kopyalanıyor..."` / `cp /mnt/target/boot/bzImage /mnt/target/boot/EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI` / `echo "\\EFI\\BOOT\\BOOTX64.EFI $ROOT_CMDLINE" > /mnt/target/boot/startup.nsh`. The working-tree file (372 lines) contains none of these; `git diff HEAD --stat` shows 325 insertions / 130 deletions.

facts.claim: No path anywhere in the repo can place a raw kernel at BOOTX64.EFI. The only write to BOOTX64.EFI in the installer copies the GRUB EFI image built at build time.
facts.evidence: os/buildroot/external/board/mcos/rootfs-overlay/usr/bin/mcos-install:269 `if cp "$BOOTLIB/BOOTX64.EFI" "$TARGET_MNT/boot/EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI"; then` (BOOTLIB=/usr/lib/mcos/boot, line 52). The kernel is copied only at line 226: `cp "$KERNEL" "$TARGET_MNT/boot/boot/bzImage"`. Repo-wide `grep -rn -i -e BOOTX64 -e EFISTUB` (excluding output/) shows BOOTX64 writes only in mcos-install:269, mkusb.sh:148/174, mkiso.sh:51/56, test-bootloader-embed.sh:76 — all grub-mkimage outputs.

facts.claim: startup.nsh no longer exists anywhere in the repository.
facts.evidence: `grep -rn "startup.nsh" . --exclude-dir=output` returned zero hits.

facts.claim: A kernel command line is ALWAYS delivered: both grub menuentries carry explicit parameters on the `linux` line, and there is no non-GRUB boot path.
facts.evidence: mcos-install:237 `CMDLINE="console=tty0 consoleblank=0 loglevel=4 fbcon=nodefer vt.global_cursor_default=0"`; line 248 `linux /boot/bzImage $CMDLINE`; line 254 (recovery) `linux /boot/bzImage console=tty0 nomodeset vga=normal loglevel=7`. Lines 301 `[ "$INSTALLED_ANY" = 1 ] || fail "hiçbir önyükleyici kurulamadı — disk boot etmez"` means an install with no bootloader aborts rather than falling back.

facts.claim: UEFI: the GRUB EFI image is built with prefix `/EFI/BOOT`, and the installer writes grub.cfg to exactly ESP:/EFI/BOOT/grub.cfg. The paths MATCH.
facts.evidence: post-build.sh:226-227 `grub-mkimage -O x86_64-efi -o "$MCOS_BOOTLIB/BOOTX64.EFI" \` / `-p /EFI/BOOT \`. mcos-install:260 `printf '%s' "$GRUB_CFG" > "$TARGET_MNT/boot/EFI/BOOT/grub.cfg" || true`, where $TARGET_MNT/boot is the mount point of the FAT boot/ESP partition (line 223 `mount "$BOOT_PART" "$TARGET_MNT/boot"`).

facts.claim: BIOS: core.img prefix is `(hd0,msdos1)/boot/grub` and the installer writes grub.cfg to partition-1 path /boot/grub/grub.cfg. The paths MATCH, conditional on the installed disk being BIOS drive 0x80 (=hd0) at boot.
facts.evidence: post-build.sh:213-214 `grub-mkimage -O i386-pc -o "$MCOS_BOOTLIB/core.img" \` / `-p '(hd0,msdos1)/boot/grub' \`. mcos-install:258 `printf '%s' "$GRUB_CFG" > "$TARGET_MNT/boot/boot/grub/grub.cfg"`; partition 1 is the FAT32 boot partition (line 189 `parted -s "$TARGET" mkpart primary fat32 1MiB ...`, line 204/205 BOOT_PART=${TARGET}1).

facts.claim: The kernel/initrd paths inside grub.cfg also resolve correctly against the $root that each prefix establishes.
facts.evidence: mcos-install:226/228 place them at <boot-partition>/boot/bzImage and /boot/initrd.img; grub.cfg lines 248-249 and 254-255 reference `/boot/bzImage` and `/boot/initrd.img`. Same partition in both the UEFI (loaded-image device) and BIOS ((hd0,msdos1)) cases.

facts.claim: Both post-build.sh grub-mkimage invocations succeed on this host and produce valid images; the `/EFI/BOOT` prefix string is embedded in the EFI binary and the EFI video modules are present.
facts.evidence: Reproduced both commands verbatim in /tmp: BIOS core.img = 164797 bytes; UEFI BOOTX64.EFI = 765952 bytes, first two bytes `M Z`, `grub-file --is-x86_64-efi` -> yes, `strings -a BOOTX64.EFI | grep EFI/BOOT` -> `/EFI/BOOT`. Module presence check: efi_gop present, efi_uga present, video_bochs present, gfxterm present, all_video present (vbe absent, i386-pc-only, expected).

facts.claim: The BIOS 'dd core.img to LBA 1' scheme is byte-correct: boot.img's kernel_sector field points at LBA 1 and grub-mkimage pre-fills core.img's diskboot blocklist for a contiguous copy starting at sector 1.
facts.evidence: `dd if=/usr/lib/grub/i386-pc/boot.img bs=1 skip=92 count=8` -> `01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00` (kernel_sector = 1). core.img bytes 500..511 (the 12-byte grub_pc_bios_boot_blocklist at 0x1F4) = `02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 | 41 01 | 20 08` = start LBA 2, len 0x0141 = 321 sectors, segment 0x0820 — exactly 322 total sectors minus the first. Matches mcos-install:294 `dd if="$BOOTLIB/core.img" of="$TARGET" bs=512 seek=1 conv=notrunc`.

facts.claim: core.img (322 sectors) fits in the MBR gap, but the installer's inline comment understates its size by ~5x.
facts.evidence: Measured 164797 bytes = 322 sectors; mcos-install:291 guards `if [ "$CORE_SECTORS" -ge 2047 ]; then fail ...`. mcos-install:289 comment reads `# 2047 sektör (≈1 MB) yer var; core.img ~30 KB.`

facts.claim: Resolution on an INSTALLED system is set exclusively by `set gfxmode` + `set gfxpayload=keep` in the grub.cfg that mcos-install writes. It is capped at 1024x768.
facts.evidence: mcos-install:243 `set gfxmode=1024x768,800x600,auto`; line 247 `set gfxpayload=keep`. No `video=` parameter appears in CMDLINE (line 237) or anywhere else in the installed system.

facts.claim: The three image-producing paths disagree on gfxmode: the Makefile ISO target matches the installer (1024x768 first), mkusb.sh uses `auto` (native/preferred mode), and mkiso.sh additionally passes `video=1024x768` on the kernel command line.
facts.evidence: Makefile:179 `'set gfxmode=1024x768,800x600,auto' \`; scripts/mkusb.sh:159 `set gfxmode=auto`; scripts/mkiso.sh:29 `set gfxmode=auto` and :33 `linux /boot/bzImage console=tty0 console=ttyS0,115200 video=1024x768 loglevel=3`. `video=` appears nowhere else in the repo.

facts.claim: scripts/mkiso.sh (the only file with a `video=` kernel parameter) is not invoked by the Makefile or any other script — it is a dead/alternate path.
facts.evidence: `grep -rn "mkiso" Makefile scripts/*.sh` returns only self-references inside scripts/mkiso.sh (lines 8, 9, 68). The Makefile `iso:` target at Makefile:152-199 builds its own grub.cfg inline and calls grub-mkrescue directly (Makefile:198).

facts.claim: The kernel enables NO native KMS driver for real GPUs. Only firmware-handover framebuffers (efifb/vesafb/simplefb/simpledrm) plus VM-only DRM drivers are built in.
facts.evidence: os/buildroot/external/board/mcos/kernel.config:80-91 = CONFIG_FB=y, CONFIG_FB_EFI=y, CONFIG_FB_VESA=y, CONFIG_SYSFB=y, CONFIG_SYSFB_SIMPLEFB=y, CONFIG_DRM=y, CONFIG_DRM_FBDEV_EMULATION=y, CONFIG_DRM_SIMPLEDRM=y, CONFIG_DRM_VIRTIO_GPU=y, CONFIG_DRM_VBOXVIDEO=y, CONFIG_DRM_VMWGFX=y, CONFIG_DRM_BOCHS=y; plus CONFIG_FB_SIMPLE=y at line 216. `grep -E "I915|AMDGPU|RADEON|NOUVEAU|DRM_AST|DRM_MGAG200|DRM_QXL|DRM_CIRRUS" kernel.config` -> NONE FOUND.

facts.claim: The kernel.config itself documents that the framebuffer is whatever GRUB hands over.
facts.evidence: kernel.config:78-80 comment: `# --- Framebuffer: real-hardware video on BOTH UEFI (GOP) and BIOS (VESA) ---` / `# sysfb/simpledrm consume the framebuffer GRUB hands over (gfxpayload=keep),` / `# giving a working console + GUI on physical machines, not just QEMU virtio.`

facts.claim: Nothing in MCOS can change the video mode at runtime: the Go framebuffer layer only reads screen info, and no modesetting utility ships in the image.
facts.evidence: `grep -nE "FBIOPUT|FBIOGET|VSCREENINFO" internal/fbdev/device_linux.go` returns only line 118 `FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO` and line 122 `FBIOGET_FSCREENINFO` — no FBIOPUT. Listing the built initramfs (`zcat os/buildroot/output/images/rootfs.cpio.gz | cpio -t | grep -E "fbset|modetest|kmscon|drm"`) yields only `usr/bin/setvtrgb` and `usr/sbin/fbset`.

facts.claim: mcos-launch reads only the framebuffer HEIGHT, from /sys/class/graphics/fb0/virtual_size, and uses it solely to pick an fbterm font size. Both the sysfs parse and the fbset fallback correctly extract height.
facts.evidence: mcos-launch:93-94 `if [ -f /sys/class/graphics/fb0/virtual_size ]; then` / `FB_H=$(cat /sys/class/graphics/fb0/virtual_size 2>/dev/null | cut -d, -f2)` (virtual_size is "W,H", so -f2 is height); line 98 fallback `FB_H=$(fbset 2>/dev/null | grep geometry | awk '{print $3}')` (geometry line is "geometry W H VW VH bpp", so $3 is height); line 100 `[ -z "$FB_H" ] && FB_H=768`; lines 102-112 map height to font size 10/12/14/18/24. has_framebuffer() at line 116 checks `[ -c /dev/fb0 ] || [ -e /sys/class/graphics/fb0 ]`.

facts.claim: A display-settings screen exists only as a PNG-generating design mockup in a _test.go file; it has no live implementation.
facts.evidence: internal/fbui/mockup_test.go:321 `func TestMockupDisplaySettings(t *testing.T) {`, line 328 `u.Panel(..., "Ekran Ayarları", true)`, line 330 `u.Text(in.Min.X, y, "Çözünürlük", u.Pal.TextDim)`, line 333 `modes := []string{"1920 x 1080", "1600 x 900", "1366 x 768", "1280 x 720", "1024 x 768"}`, line 374 `save(t, img, "04-ekran-ayarlari.png")`. `grep -rn "Ekran Ayar" --include="*.go" . | grep -v _test` returns zero hits. internal/fbui contains only mockup_test.go, theme.go, widgets.go.

facts.claim: The FAT boot partition is never mounted at runtime, so any settings screen that rewrites grub.cfg must mount it itself.
facts.evidence: os/buildroot/external/board/mcos/rootfs-overlay/etc/fstab contains only proc, devtmpfs, devpts, tmpfs /tmp, tmpfs /run, sysfs — no /boot entry. etc/init.d/S99mcos:17-35 `mount_persistent()` mounts only the MCOS-DATA label at /data (line 29 `part="$(/usr/bin/mcos-findfs MCOS-DATA 2>/dev/null || true)"`, line 35 `if mount "$part" "$MCOS_DATA"; then`).

facts.claim: scripts/test-install-logic.sh passes today but contains NO check for a kernel-at-BOOTX64.EFI regression, no startup.nsh check, and no check that grub.cfg's path matches the GRUB prefix.
facts.evidence: Ran `sh scripts/test-install-logic.sh` -> `SONUC: TUM TESTLER GECTI`. Section 4 (lines 102-147) checks only: root= count == 0, `initrd /boot/initrd.img` count == 2, MCOS-DATA present, grub-install count == 0, grub-mkimage count == 0, /usr/lib/mcos/boot present, boot.img present, core.img present, INSTALLED_ANY present, verify_fail present, `cp -a /data/.` present, executable bit. `grep -c` over the file for BOOTX64, EFI/BOOT, startup, prefix -> none of these strings appear.

facts.claim: scripts/verify-usb.sh cannot catch either regression: it only tests that a file named BOOTX64 exists, and its grub.cfg check greps a RECURSIVE directory listing so a grub.cfg at any path satisfies a check labelled '/EFI/BOOT/grub.cfg'.
facts.evidence: verify-usb.sh:96 `FATLIST="$(mdir -i "$MT" -a -/ :: 2>/dev/null)"` (-/ = recursive); lines 107-113 `check_file() { if printf '%s\n' "$FATLIST" | grep -qi "$1"; then ok ...`; line 118 `check_file 'BOOTX64'  "UEFI önyükleyici (/EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI)"`; line 119 `check_file 'grub *cfg' "GRUB yapılandırması (/EFI/BOOT/grub.cfg)"`. No content/type inspection of BOOTX64.EFI anywhere in the file.

facts.claim: A magic-byte check would not distinguish a raw kernel from a GRUB EFI image — both begin with 'MZ'. The existing MZ check in test-bootloader-embed.sh therefore provides no protection against the old regression.
facts.evidence: `head -c 2 /tmp/grubprobe2/BOOTX64.EFI | od -An -c` -> `M Z`; `head -c 2 os/buildroot/output/images/bzImage | od -An -c` -> `M Z`. scripts/test-bootloader-embed.sh:81-85 `MZ="$(dd if="$W/BOOTX64.EFI" bs=2 count=1 status=none | od -An -c | tr -d ' \n')"` / `case "$MZ" in *M*Z*) ok "gecerli PE/COFF imzasi (MZ)" ;;`.

facts.claim: The current Buildroot output tree is stale and does not contain the embedded bootloader files, so an install run from the currently built image would abort.
facts.evidence: `ls os/buildroot/output/target/usr/lib/mcos` -> 'No such file or directory'. `zcat os/buildroot/output/images/rootfs.cpio.gz | cpio -t | grep -c usr/lib/mcos` -> 0, while the same listing does contain `usr/bin/mcos-install`. Timestamps: post-build.sh = 2026-09-10 20:38:47, images/rootfs.cpio.gz = 2026-09-10 16:57:34, images/bzImage = 2026-09-10 16:52:31. mcos-install:126-131 would then fail with 'önyükleyici dosyaları imajda yok'. The host has grub-mkimage and /usr/lib/grub/{i386-pc,x86_64-efi}, so a rebuild will populate it.

facts.claim: The `&&`-chained guards in mcos-install are safe under `set -eu` (they do not cause a silent early exit).
facts.evidence: Tested the exact patterns from mcos-install:126-127 and :156-159 under dash: `dash -c 'set -eu; H=0; [ -f /nonexistent1 ] && [ -f /nonexistent2 ] && H=1; echo survived'` -> 'survived, H=0'; the loop `[ -n "$I" ] && break` pattern also survived both iterations.

facts.claim: On VMs the kernel does have real KMS drivers, so runtime modesetting is theoretically possible there even though no userspace tool ships to do it.
facts.evidence: kernel.config:88-91 CONFIG_DRM_VIRTIO_GPU=y, CONFIG_DRM_VBOXVIDEO=y, CONFIG_DRM_VMWGFX=y, CONFIG_DRM_BOCHS=y. I did not boot a VM to confirm mode changes actually take effect.

problems.title: EFI grub.cfg write failure is swallowed and never verified — silent boot-to-rescue on UEFI
problems.why_wrong: The BIOS copy of grub.cfg is written with `|| fail` (line 258), but the UEFI copy at line 260 ends in `|| true`, and the final verification block checks `/boot/bzImage`, `/boot/initrd.img`, `/boot/grub/grub.cfg` and `BOOTX64.EFI` — but never `/EFI/BOOT/grub.cfg`. Since the EFI GRUB image's prefix is `/EFI/BOOT`, that file is the ONLY config UEFI GRUB will load. If its write fails, the installer reports 100% success and the disk boots UEFI into GRUB's minimal prompt with no menu and no kernel.
problems.failure_scenario: Boot partition fills up while copying the ~122 MB initrd plus the 10 MB kernel (BOOT_MB is sized from kernel+initrd+16 MB, line 165-166, leaving little slack). The `printf > /EFI/BOOT/grub.cfg` at line 260 fails with ENOSPC; `|| true` discards it; line 348 only checks `/boot/grub/grub.cfg`, which was written earlier and exists. Install reports 'Kurulum tamamlandı (BIOS + UEFI)'. On a UEFI machine the user gets a bare `grub>` prompt.

problems.title: BIOS core.img hardcodes (hd0,msdos1) and the generated grub.cfg never runs `search --set=root`
problems.why_wrong: The BIOS prefix `(hd0,msdos1)/boot/grub` binds the config location to BIOS drive 0x80. The installer's grub.cfg contains no `search` command, unlike the Makefile ISO config which does `search --no-floppy --set=root --file /boot/bzImage` (Makefile:184/190). If firmware does not map the installed USB to 0x80, GRUB cannot locate its own prefix and drops to rescue. The fix costs one line: the `search`, `search_fs_file` and `search_label` modules are already embedded in core.img (post-build.sh:215-216), and mkfs.vfat already labels the partition MCOS-BOOT (mcos-install:213).
problems.failure_scenario: User installs MCOS to a USB stick on a desktop that also has an internal SATA disk, then boots the USB via the BIOS boot menu on a firmware that keeps the internal disk as 0x80 and assigns the USB 0x81. boot.img + core.img load from the USB's MBR, but core.img then resolves `(hd0,msdos1)/boot/grub/grub.cfg` to the internal disk's first partition, finds nothing, and lands at `grub rescue>`.

problems.title: Installed grub.cfg sets `terminal_output gfxterm` only — no console fallback if gfxterm cannot initialize
problems.why_wrong: The config does `insmod all_video` / `insmod gfxterm` / `set gfxmode=1024x768,800x600,auto` / `terminal_output gfxterm`. Redirecting output exclusively to gfxterm means that if no graphics mode can be established, GRUB's menu renders nowhere. The Makefile ISO config for the same build deliberately keeps both: Makefile:180-181 `'terminal_input console' \` / `'terminal_output console gfxterm' \`. The installer is strictly less robust than the ISO it was launched from, on the same hardware.
problems.failure_scenario: UEFI firmware whose GOP advertises no mode matching 1024x768 or 800x600 and where `auto` also fails to produce a usable gfxterm; or a BIOS whose VBE is unusable. GRUB loads and times out after 3 seconds on a black screen — the user sees nothing and cannot pick the recovery entry.

problems.title: Neither verify-usb.sh nor test-install-logic.sh nor test-bootloader-embed.sh can detect a kernel-at-BOOTX64.EFI regression or a grub.cfg/prefix mismatch
problems.why_wrong: verify-usb.sh:118 only asserts that some entry matching 'BOOTX64' appears in the FAT listing — it never inspects the file, and a raw bzImage even shares GRUB's 'MZ' PE magic (measured), so the existing MZ assertion in test-bootloader-embed.sh:81-85 would also pass. verify-usb.sh:119's `check_file 'grub *cfg'` greps a recursive listing produced by `mdir -a -/ ::` (line 96), so a grub.cfg at /boot/grub satisfies a check labelled '/EFI/BOOT/grub.cfg' and vice versa — a prefix/path mismatch is invisible. test-install-logic.sh's mcos-install invariants section never mentions BOOTX64, EFI/BOOT, startup.nsh, or any prefix.
problems.failure_scenario: Someone reintroduces `cp $KERNEL .../EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI` as a fallback, or changes post-build.sh's UEFI prefix from `/EFI/BOOT` to `/boot/grub` without moving the installer's write. Both test scripts print 'TUM TESTLER GECTI' / 'TÜM KONTROLLER GEÇTİ' and the regression ships.

problems.title: verify-usb.sh infers firmware mode from the partition-table type, so it checks the wrong things on any mcos-install-produced disk
problems.why_wrong: Lines 33-37 set MODE=uefi for a gpt label and MODE=bios for a dos label. mcos-install deliberately creates an MBR/msdos table (line 188 `parted -s "$TARGET" mklabel msdos`, with the design comment at lines 170-173 explaining that one MBR disk serves both firmwares) while installing BOTH BIOS and UEFI bootloaders. verify-usb.sh therefore takes the BIOS branch, checks for syslinux artifacts that mcos-install never writes (lines 121-125: ldlinux.sys, ldlinux.c32, menu.c32, libcom32, syslinux.cfg), and skips the BOOTX64.EFI check entirely (line 118).
problems.failure_scenario: An operator images an mcos-install-produced USB and runs `scripts/verify-usb.sh disk.img` to confirm it. The script prints five spurious HATA lines for missing syslinux modules and exits 1, while never once verifying the UEFI bootloader that is actually present. A genuinely missing BOOTX64.EFI would go unreported.

problems.title: Resolution is hard-capped at 1024x768 on installed systems and is inconsistent with the USB image path
problems.why_wrong: `set gfxmode=1024x768,800x600,auto` makes GRUB pick 1024x768 whenever the firmware can provide it, so `auto` (native/preferred mode) is only ever reached as a third fallback. Because no native KMS driver is built in (verified: no i915/amdgpu/radeon/nouveau in kernel.config) and only efifb/vesafb/simpledrm consume the bootloader handover, this single line fixes the display resolution for the entire life of the installed system. scripts/mkusb.sh:159 uses `set gfxmode=auto` for the same hardware, so the same machine gets a higher resolution from a mkusb image than from an installed disk.
problems.failure_scenario: User with a 1920x1080 panel installs MCOS. GRUB's efi_gop finds a 1024x768 mode, sets it, and hands it to the kernel via gfxpayload=keep. simpledrm/efifb expose exactly that one mode; fbset (present at usr/sbin/fbset) cannot change it; mcos-launch reads FB_H=768 and selects a 14px fbterm font. The user has no way to reach 1080p short of reinstalling or hand-editing grub.cfg on an unmounted FAT partition.

problems.title: The 'recovery' menu entry can never display the TUI panel
problems.why_wrong: The recovery entry sets `gfxpayload=text` and passes `nomodeset`, which yields a VGA text console with no /dev/fb0. mcos-launch:155 gates the panel on `[ -x /usr/bin/fbterm ] && has_framebuffer()` (line 116: `[ -c /dev/fb0 ] || [ -e /sys/class/graphics/fb0 ]`), so this entry always lands in show_recovery() with 'framebuffer veya fbterm bulunamadi'. That may be intended for a rescue path, but it is not documented as such and the menu label ('kurtarma — VGA metin modu, ayrıntılı günlük') suggests a usable degraded UI rather than no UI.
problems.failure_scenario: Graphics trouble on the default entry sends the user to the recovery entry expecting a text-mode panel. They instead get a bare shell-adjacent recovery menu with no MCOS UI at all, and no on-screen explanation that this entry structurally cannot start the panel.

problems.title: Stale inline comment understates core.img size by ~5x, weakening the MBR-gap reasoning
problems.why_wrong: The comment reads '2047 sektör (≈1 MB) yer var; core.img ~30 KB.' The actual core.img built from post-build.sh:213-217's module list measures 164797 bytes = 322 sectors (~161 KB). The runtime guard at line 291 is correct and the image still fits comfortably, but the comment invites a future contributor to add modules under the false impression of a 30x margin when the real margin is ~6x.
problems.failure_scenario: A contributor adds several modules (e.g. lvm, luks, btrfs, xfs, a font) to the i386-pc list believing there is ~1 MB of headroom against a 30 KB baseline. core.img crosses 2047 sectors, and instead of a build-time signal the failure surfaces at install time as `fail "core.img MBR boşluğuna sığmıyor"` on a user's machine.

problems.title: post-build.sh still advertises an EFISTUB fallback that no longer exists
problems.why_wrong: The warning printed when BOOTX64.EFI generation fails reads 'UYARI - BOOTX64.EFI uretilemedi; USB'ye kurulum UEFI'de EFISTUB'a duser'. There is no EFISTUB path left in mcos-install; the real behaviour is that HAVE_UEFI stays 0 (mcos-install:127) and the disk becomes BIOS-only, or the install aborts at line 129-131 if BIOS is also unavailable. The message describes exactly the broken behaviour that was removed.
problems.failure_scenario: A build on a host lacking grub-efi-amd64-bin prints this warning. The maintainer reads it as 'UEFI still works via EFISTUB' and ships the image; UEFI-only machines then simply refuse to boot the installed disk, with no diagnostic pointing at the missing package.

problems.title: Test-script module lists are duplicated from post-build.sh and can drift silently
problems.why_wrong: MODULES_PC and MODULES_EFI are hand-copied from post-build.sh:215-217 and :228-230, guarded only by the comment 'post-build.sh ile AYNI modül listeleri. Değiştirirseniz orayı da güncelleyin.' Nothing enforces the equality, so the test can pass against a module list that the build no longer uses — which is precisely the class of silent failure the script's own header (lines 5-9) says it exists to prevent.
problems.failure_scenario: Someone removes `search_fs_file` from post-build.sh's EFI list to shrink the image but forgets test-bootloader-embed.sh. The test keeps building and validating the old list, reports success, and a later grub.cfg that relies on `search --file` fails only on real hardware.

recommendations: Make the UEFI grub.cfg write authoritative: change mcos-install:260 from `|| true` to `|| fail "EFI grub.cfg yazılamadı"`, and add `[ -f "$TARGET_MNT/boot/EFI/BOOT/grub.cfg" ] || verify_fail="EFI grub.cfg yok"` inside the verification block at mcos-install:349-351 next to the existing BOOTX64.EFI check. This is the only config UEFI GRUB reads, and today it is the one boot-critical file nothing checks.

Add `search --no-floppy --set=root --label MCOS-BOOT` (or `--file /boot/bzImage`) as the first line of each menuentry in the grub.cfg that mcos-install writes (lines 246-256), mirroring Makefile:184/190. The `search`, `search_fs_file` and `search_label` modules are already embedded in both core.img and BOOTX64.EFI, and mkfs.vfat already sets the MCOS-BOOT label, so this removes the `(hd0,msdos1)` dependency at zero cost.

Change mcos-install:244 to `terminal_output console gfxterm` and add `terminal_input console`, matching the ISO config at Makefile:180-181, so the menu remains visible when no graphics mode can be established.

To raise resolution: edit the gfxmode list at mcos-install:243 to `set gfxmode=1920x1080,1600x900,1366x768,1280x720,1024x768,auto` and keep `gfxpayload=keep`. Apply the same change to Makefile:179 so the live ISO and the installed system agree, and reconcile scripts/mkusb.sh:159 (`auto`) with whichever policy you pick. No kernel change is needed — efi_gop/efi_uga are already embedded in BOOTX64.EFI, and CONFIG_FB_EFI/SYSFB/SIMPLEDRM already consume the handover.

Do NOT plan a live resolution switcher against the current kernel: with no i915/amdgpu/radeon/nouveau built in, bare-metal displays run on efifb/vesafb/simpledrm, which expose exactly the one mode the bootloader set. A 'Ekran Ayarları' screen must (a) enumerate candidate modes, (b) locate the boot partition via `/usr/bin/mcos-findfs MCOS-BOOT` and mount it — nothing mounts it at runtime, per fstab and S99mcos:17-35, (c) rewrite BOTH /boot/grub/grub.cfg and /EFI/BOOT/grub.cfg, and (d) tell the user a reboot is required. The mockup at internal/fbui/mockup_test.go:321-375 is a good starting point but its 'Uygula' button cannot take effect without a restart; label it accordingly.

If you want genuine runtime modesetting later, that is a kernel-config change (add CONFIG_DRM_I915 / CONFIG_DRM_AMDGPU / CONFIG_DRM_NOUVEAU plus the firmware blobs) and a userspace KMS tool — a much larger change than the gfxmode edit, and it will grow the initramfs well beyond its current ~122 MB.

Add two regression assertions to scripts/test-install-logic.sh section 4: (1) `grep -c 'BOOTX64.EFI' on lines that also mention $KERNEL or bzImage` must be 0, and a `grep -c 'startup.nsh'` must be 0 — this is the exact regression that produced the empty-cmdline VFS panic; (2) assert that the grub.cfg destination path in mcos-install matches the `-p` prefix in post-build.sh, e.g. extract `-p /EFI/BOOT` from post-build.sh and require mcos-install to write `$prefix/grub.cfg`. Neither check exists today.

Fix scripts/verify-usb.sh so it can validate mcos-install output: derive the firmware mode from what is actually on the FAT partition (presence of /EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI and/or a nonzero MBR bootstrap) rather than from the partition-table label at lines 33-37, since mcos-install always writes an msdos table while installing both bootloaders. Also replace the recursive-listing greps at lines 118-119 with path-exact `mdir -i "$MT" ::/EFI/BOOT` lookups so a misplaced grub.cfg is caught, and add a type check on BOOTX64.EFI stronger than MZ magic (a raw bzImage also starts with MZ) — `grub-file --is-x86_64-efi` on an extracted copy, or a grep for the embedded prefix string.

Update the two stale comments: mcos-install:289 ('core.img ~30 KB' -> ~161 KB / 322 sectors as measured) and post-build.sh:234 (drop the EFISTUB claim; say the install will be BIOS-only or will abort, and name the missing `grub-efi-amd64-bin` package).

Rebuild before any boot testing: os/buildroot/output/target/usr/lib/mcos does not exist and the built rootfs.cpio.gz contains zero usr/lib/mcos entries, so the currently built image will abort at mcos-install:130 with 'önyükleyici dosyaları imajda yok'. The host has grub-mkimage and both /usr/lib/grub platforms, so a plain rebuild populates it.

Consider deleting or wiring up scripts/mkiso.sh — it is referenced by nothing (the Makefile `iso:` target builds its own grub.cfg inline) and it is the only file carrying a `video=1024x768` kernel parameter, which will mislead anyone grepping for the resolution knob.

surveys.summary: The OOBE wizard has several concrete logic defects, the worst being that pressing Enter on the "KURULUM BAŞARILI" screen re-runs the disk install instead of rebooting, and that a successful disk install hard-reboots at step 5/10 so the wizard's last five steps and the entire config save (doSetupSave) never run. Additional verified defects: "Geri" is advertised but is a no-op on steps 2–5, the required PC name is never persisted anywhere, the required "Düğüm adı" field cannot accept 'h', 'l' or space, the Wi-Fi list renders only 8 networks while the cursor can move past them, and several errors (disk-list RPC, UpdateConfig, Persist) are swallowed with no user-visible feedback.

facts.claim: The wizard has exactly 10 steps (stepIntro..stepConfirm) and stepCount == 10, so the "adım N/10" counter and progress percentage are arithmetically correct.
facts.evidence: panel/view_setup.go:26-38 (const block, stepCount last) and panel/view_setup.go:620 `pct := (int(s.step) + 1) * 100 / int(stepCount)`

facts.claim: The install-target index mapping is correct — there is NO off-by-one with the trailing "Atla" row. The view renders disks at cursor==i and advance() uses s.disks[s.cursor] guarded by `s.cursor < len(s.disks)`.
facts.evidence: panel/view_setup.go:735-748 (`for i, d := range s.disks` ... `if s.cursor == i`) and panel/view_setup.go:411-416 (`if s.cursor < len(s.disks) { disk := s.disks[s.cursor] ... }`)

facts.claim: Choosing "Atla" (cursor == len(disks)) does NOT start an install; it falls through to `s.goTo(stepTheme)`.
facts.evidence: panel/view_setup.go:411-417 — the `if s.cursor < len(s.disks)` branch is skipped, then `s.goTo(stepTheme)`

facts.claim: With zero disks found the user is not stuck: fieldCount()==3 (skip row + 2 checkboxes), cursor 0 is the "Atla" row, and Enter advances to stepTheme. No index panic is possible (all cursor arithmetic is modulo a positive count).
facts.evidence: panel/view_setup.go:364-372 `case stepInstall: return len(s.disks) + 1 + 2`, panel/view_setup.go:411-417

facts.claim: 'r' (rescan) does NOT conflict with typing in the PC-name field. updateIdentity only treats 'r' as rescan when cursor != 0; at cursor 0 it falls through to pcName.Update.
facts.evidence: panel/view_setup.go:273-277 `if m.String() == "r" && s.cursor != 0 { ... }`; panel/view_setup.go:322-327 fall-through to `s.pcName.Update(m)`

facts.claim: The Java step is NOT a dead end without internet: viewJava renders "Kurulu Java bulunamadı." plus an informational message and Enter always advances to stepInstall; there is no gate.
facts.evidence: panel/view_setup.go:893-914 (viewJava) and panel/view_setup.go:408-410 (`case stepJava: s.goTo(stepInstall)`) — no condition on s.javaOK or s.status

facts.claim: The daemon's Wi-Fi scan returns an uncapped list of unique SSIDs (no limit of 8), so >8 networks is realistic in practice.
facts.evidence: internal/netcfg/netcfg_linux.go:146-153 — appends every unique SSID to allNets with no cap

facts.claim: The IPC client serializes every call under a mutex, so concurrent panel commands cannot interleave responses; but no deadline is set, so a slow daemon call blocks all other RPCs.
facts.evidence: internal/ipc/client.go:62-64 `c.mu.Lock(); defer c.mu.Unlock()` and roundtrip() at internal/ipc/client.go:100-113 with no SetDeadline

facts.claim: model.Config has no hostname/PC-name field at all; the only Hostname fields in the codebase are read-only system info or tunnel addresses.
facts.evidence: internal/model/config.go:67-90 (full Config struct — no hostname) and `grep -rn ostname` hits only internal/model/system.go:58 (SystemStatus.Net.Hostname), tunnel.go, model.go

facts.claim: handleConfigSet replaces the whole config document (only Cluster.Secret is preserved from the previous value).
facts.evidence: internal/daemon/handlers.go:123-148 — decodes a full model.Config, restores prevSecret only, then store.SaveConfig(d.cfgPath, &cfg)

facts.claim: mcos-install copies /data (config.json, downloaded Java) onto the new MCOS-DATA partition, but the OOBE has not written config.json yet at that point because doSetupSave only runs at stepConfirm.
facts.evidence: os/buildroot/.../usr/bin/mcos-install:305-325 (`cp -a /data/. "$TARGET_MNT/"`, with a comment claiming OOBE settings live in /data) vs panel/view_setup.go:427-429 (`case stepConfirm: return true, doSetupSave(...)`)

facts.claim: Bubble Tea v1.3.10 reports a space keypress as KeyType KeySpace whose String() is " ", so the wizard's `case "right", "l", " ":` really does intercept the space bar.
facts.evidence: ~/go/pkg/mod/github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea@v1.3.10/key.go:302 `KeySpace: " "` and key.go:698-701 (single ' ' rune becomes KeySpace)

problems.title: Enter on the "KURULUM BAŞARILI" screen re-runs the disk installation instead of rebooting
problems.why_wrong: After installDoneMsg succeeds, handleInstallDone sets s.loading=false and s.installSuccess=true but never resets s.cursor, which still points at the installed disk index (0..len(disks)-1). The success screen renders RenderButton(th, "Hemen Yeniden Başlat", "Enter", true), promising a reboot. But update() is no longer short-circuited by s.loading, step is still stepInstall, so "enter" routes to advance() -> `case stepInstall: if s.cursor < len(s.disks) { ... doInstallOS(...) }`. Nothing in the stepInstall branch knows about installSuccess.
problems.failure_scenario: User picks /dev/sda, install finishes, screen says "[OK] KURULUM BAŞARILI! Lütfen MCOS kurulum USB'sini ŞİMDİ ÇIKARIN" with a "Hemen Yeniden Başlat  Enter" button and a 10-second countdown. User presses Enter (as instructed) to reboot immediately. Instead the panel flips back to "[>>] KURULUM DEVAM EDİYOR" and runs `mcos-install /dev/sda` a second time, re-partitioning and re-formatting the freshly installed disk. If the user already pulled the USB as told, the second run is executing from a half-removed medium. Left/right/space on that same screen also silently toggle the dlJava/dlPlugins checkboxes, and up/down move the disk cursor.

problems.title: A successful disk install ends the wizard at step 5/10 — steps 6–10 and doSetupSave are unreachable, so nothing the wizard collected is ever persisted
problems.why_wrong: doSetupSave — the only call to cl.UpdateConfig — runs exclusively from `case stepConfirm` (step 9). stepInstall is step 4 (displayed as "adım 5/10"). When the install succeeds the model starts a 10s countdown and then executes `reboot -f`. stepTheme, stepBudget, stepCluster, stepFirstServer and stepConfirm are therefore never reached on the install path, so cfg.Theme, cfg.Timezone, cfg.Budget, cfg.Cluster.*, cfg.WiFiSSID/WiFiPassword, cfg.SetupComplete and cfg.HardwareID are never written. mcos-install's own comment (lines 306-308) explicitly assumes the OOBE settings already exist in /data as config.json — they do not.
problems.failure_scenario: User walks through Intro, System, Wi-Fi and Java, reaches "adım 5/10 · Diske Kurulum", selects a disk, install succeeds, the box hard-reboots. On the installed system config.json is absent (or a bare default), SetupComplete is false, so the full 10-step wizard starts again from scratch — including the Wi-Fi password the user already typed. The wizard's progress bar told them they were halfway through a 10-step flow that in fact terminates at step 5.

problems.title: "Geri" (Shift+Tab) is shown in the action bar on steps 2–5 but is a silent no-op there
problems.why_wrong: The action bar appends `Action{Label: "Geri", Key: "Shift+Tab"}` whenever `s.step > stepIntro`, i.e. on stepSystem(1), stepIdentity(2), stepJava(3) and stepInstall(4) as well. back() only does anything when `s.step > stepInstall`, i.e. on steps 5..9. On steps 1–4 the key is consumed and nothing happens — no movement, no error message.
problems.failure_scenario: On "Java Sürücüleri" (adım 4/10) the user realises they picked the wrong Wi-Fi network and presses Shift+Tab, which the on-screen button bar says is "Geri". The screen does not change at all. The user presses it repeatedly; the only way back to the network step is Esc, which cancels the entire wizard (s.cancelled=true, a.setup=nil).

problems.title: The PC name is mandatory and shown in the summary but is never persisted anywhere
problems.why_wrong: proceedFromIdentity refuses to advance with `errMsg = "PC adı gerekli"` when pcName is blank, and viewConfirm prints `s.kv("PC adı", s.pcName.Value())`. But buildConfig() never reads s.pcName, there is no hostname field in model.Config (internal/model/config.go:67-90), and no RPC anywhere sets a hostname. The value is used only for a validation gate and a cosmetic summary line.
problems.failure_scenario: User types "salon-pc" as the PC name, is blocked from continuing until they do, sees "PC adı  salon-pc" on the confirmation screen, presses Enter to finish. After setup the panel's Donanım tab still shows the kernel-default hostname; the name is gone. Re-running the wizard asks for it again and discards it again.

problems.title: The required "Düğüm adı" field cannot accept 'h', 'l', or space, and the caret cannot be moved with the arrow keys
problems.location: panel/view_setup.go:192-197 (update key switch) with panel/view_setup.go:209-221 (activeTextInput) and panel/view_setup.go:419-424 (cluster validation)
problems.why_wrong: update() routes only stepIdentity to a dedicated handler; every other step goes through the generic switch, where `case "left", "h":` and `case "right", "l", " ":` call adjust() and `return false, nil` unconditionally. On stepCluster with cursor==1 (the focused nodeName textinput) adjust() does nothing (it only acts on cursor==0), so those keystrokes are swallowed before reaching activeTextInput()/ti.Update(m). nodeName's "mcos-1" is only a Placeholder, so Value() starts empty and advance() blocks with "Düğüm adı gerekli" until the user types something.
problems.failure_scenario: On "Cihaz Eşleştirme" the user moves to "Düğüm adı" and types "salon" — the 'l' is dropped and the field reads "saon". Typing "home lab" yields "omeab" (h, space and l all swallowed). They cannot press Left/Right to fix the middle of the string either. The only way forward is a name containing none of h, l or space.

problems.title: Wi-Fi list renders at most 8 networks but the cursor can move onto rows 9..N, which are invisible
problems.location: panel/view_setup.go:228 (identityRows) vs panel/view_setup.go:873-880 (view loop with `if i >= 8 { break }`)
problems.why_wrong: identityRows() returns `1 + len(s.networks) + 1` with no cap, and updateIdentity's up/down wrap modulo that count. viewIdentity only draws the first 8 networks. For rows 9..len(networks) nothing is drawn as selected — the PC-name row is not highlighted, no network row is highlighted, and isWiredRow() is false — so the highlight simply vanishes from the screen while networkAt(cursor) still returns a real (undrawn) AP.
problems.failure_scenario: In an apartment block the scan returns 14 SSIDs. The user presses ↓ ten times: after the 9th press the selection marker disappears from the screen entirely (rows 9-14 are not rendered). Pressing Enter opens the "… Parolası:" prompt for an SSID whose name is never shown, or connects directly to an unnamed open network. Pressing ↓ four more times wraps back to the PC-name row, so the user cannot tell how many hidden rows exist.

problems.title: The "Temel sunucu dosyalarını (Paper/Fabric) önceden indir" checkbox does nothing
problems.why_wrong: doInstallOS takes dlPlugins as a parameter but never reads it; the body only honours dlJava and then execs mcos-install. The source even says so: "Note: dlPlugins logic can be added here or in mcos-install script." The checkbox defaults to checked (newSetup sets dlPlugins: true), so every user is shown a ticked box for a feature that is not implemented.
problems.failure_scenario: User leaves "☑ Temel sunucu dosyalarını (Paper/Fabric) önceden indir" checked on a metered connection, expecting the jars to be cached for offline use. Install reports success. Later, offline, creating a Paper server fails to download anything because nothing was pre-fetched.

problems.title: The "Java 17 ve 21 sürümlerini şimdi indir" option is only honoured on the disk-install path, and its failures are discarded
problems.why_wrong: The two `cl.JavaInstall(...)` calls live inside doInstallOS, which is invoked only when `s.cursor < len(s.disks)`. Taking "Atla" jumps straight to stepTheme, so the checked box downloads nothing. Both calls also discard their error (`_, _ = cl.JavaInstall(17)`), so a DNS/TLS failure (very likely on an RTC-less box whose clock is not yet synced — see the unimplemented clock gate) is invisible and the install still reports success.
problems.failure_scenario: User ticks "Java 17 ve 21 sürümlerini şimdi indir", then chooses "Atla (Sadece RAM'de çalıştır)" because they do not want to wipe a disk. No Java is downloaded and no message says so. Variant: user does install to disk with no internet — both JavaInstall calls fail silently, the install proceeds, and the screen shows "[OK] KURULUM BAŞARILI".

problems.title: Disk-enumeration RPC errors are dropped; an RPC failure is indistinguishable from "no disks found"
problems.why_wrong: doFetchDisks packages `err` into disksMsg, but the handler assigns `a.setup.disks = m.disks` and clears disksLoading without ever inspecting m.err. viewInstall then renders an empty disk list with only the "Atla" row and the reassuring "MCOS'u kalıcı olarak kuracağınız diski seçin:" heading.
problems.failure_scenario: The daemon's system.disks call fails (or the IPC connection dropped and the retry failed). The user sees the install screen with zero disks listed, concludes their SSD is unsupported, and picks "Atla", ending up on a RAM-only system. No error is ever shown, and pressing 'r' to rescan produces the same silent empty list.

problems.title: A failure to save the configuration on the final step is completely invisible
problems.why_wrong: doSetupSave returns errMsg{err} when cl.UpdateConfig fails. app.go's errMsg case only sets `a.statusErr`, and View() returns `a.setup.view(...)` as soon as a.setup != nil — the main layout that renders statusErr is never drawn while the wizard is open. setupDoneMsg is never emitted, so a.setup stays non-nil and the user remains on the confirmation screen with no error text. Separately, `_, _ = cl.Persist("")` discards its error entirely, yet setupDoneMsg still flashes "✓ kurulum tamamlandı".
problems.failure_scenario: On the "Kurulum Onayı" screen the user presses Enter ("Kurulumu Bitir"). The config write fails (read-only /data, disk full, daemon error). The screen does not change — same summary, no error, no spinner. The user presses Enter again and again, firing a fresh UpdateConfig each time. Alternatively the config saves but mcos-persist fails; the user is told "✓ kurulum tamamlandı", reboots, and every setting is gone.

problems.title: Re-running the wizard from Settings overwrites the whole config with defaults, silently resetting Turbo / autostart / features / tier
problems.location: panel/app.go:422-425 and panel/app.go:578-581 (newSetup on 'i' / Settings row 3) with panel/view_setup.go:493-511 (buildConfig)
problems.why_wrong: buildConfig() starts from `model.DefaultConfig()` and only fills in theme, timezone, budget, cluster and Wi-Fi. handleConfigSet replaces the stored document wholesale (only Cluster.Secret survives). newSetup() never loads the existing config, so every other live setting is reset: Turbo -> false (read at internal/daemon/handlers.go:92,103,522), AutostartServers -> true (read at internal/daemon/daemon.go:382), WAN.Autostart -> false, Features -> all auto, Tier.Override -> cleared, NodeID -> regenerated.
problems.failure_scenario: User has Turbo ON and autostart OFF. They open Ayarlar and press 'i' just to change the timezone. Completing the wizard writes a default-derived config: Turbo is now off and all servers will autostart on next boot. Nothing in the wizard mentions these settings, so the user has no way to know they were changed.

problems.title: The documented Java gate on internet + clock sync is not implemented; s.status is dead and a fixed 2-second sleep stands in for NTP
problems.why_wrong: The struct comment says "status mirrors the daemon's live status so the Java step can gate on internet + clock sync (RTC-less PCs need NTP before any TLS download)", and internal/daemon/handlers_system.go:236-239 says "the OOBE gates Java behind ClockSynced". Grepping view_setup.go shows s.status is written at app.go:129 and read nowhere. Instead proceedFromIdentity does a hardcoded `time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)` before calling cl.JavaList(), and viewJava never consults net.Internet or status.ClockSynced.
problems.failure_scenario: An RTC-less mini-PC boots with a 1970 clock. The user connects Wi-Fi; 2 seconds later JavaList runs, NTP has not completed, and the Java step just reports "Kurulu Java bulunamadı." and lets the user continue. Ticking "Java 17 ve 21 indir" on the next screen then fails TLS certificate validation against the wrong date — and, per the finding above, that failure is discarded and the install still reports success.

problems.title: A late javaSetupMsg clears s.loading in the middle of a disk install, re-enabling input and allowing a concurrent second install
problems.why_wrong: handleJavaSetup clears s.loading regardless of what set it. The only producer of javaSetupMsg is proceedFromIdentity's command, which can run for a long time (cl.WiFiApply serialises behind the IPC mutex and can block on DHCP, plus a fixed 2s sleep, plus cl.JavaList). update()'s `if s.loading { return false, nil }` guard is the only thing blocking keystrokes during an install.
problems.failure_scenario: User enters a Wi-Fi password; WiFiApply blocks for ~30s waiting on DHCP. Meanwhile the user presses Enter through the Java step and the install step and starts installing to /dev/sda (s.loading = true). The delayed javaSetupMsg then arrives, sets s.loading = false, and the keyboard is live again during the install. Enter now re-enters `case stepInstall` and launches a second `mcos-install /dev/sda` concurrently with the first.

problems.title: A disk is wiped on a single Enter with no confirmation step, and 'Geri' from the theme step drops the user back onto that screen with the cursor on disk 0
problems.why_wrong: advance() calls doInstallOS immediately on Enter; the only warning is a static red line at the bottom of the list. back() from stepTheme does `s.step--` into stepInstall and resets s.cursor to 0, which is the first disk row — so the primary action on that freshly-entered screen is "wipe the first disk".
problems.failure_scenario: User is on "Görünüm ve Zaman" (adım 6/10) having chosen "Atla" on the install step. They press Shift+Tab to double-check something, landing back on "Diske Kurulum" with the selection marker on /dev/sda. Reflexively pressing Enter (the wizard's universal "continue" key, which advanced them on every prior screen) immediately begins repartitioning /dev/sda with no confirmation prompt.

problems.title: Enter on the "Ek Seçenekler" checkbox rows silently skips the disk install
problems.location: panel/view_setup.go:411-417 (advance) and panel/view_setup.go:768-790 (checkbox rows at cursor len(disks)+1 and +2)
problems.why_wrong: The checkbox rows are toggled with ←/→/space (adjust, panel/view_setup.go:453-458). Enter on those rows fails the `s.cursor < len(s.disks)` test and falls into `s.goTo(stepTheme)` — the same outcome as choosing "Atla" — with no indication that the disk install was skipped.
problems.failure_scenario: User selects /dev/sda, then moves down to "☑ Java 17 ve 21 sürümlerini şimdi indir" to verify it is ticked, and presses Enter expecting to continue with the selected disk. The wizard jumps to "Görünüm ve Zaman" and no install ever happens; the user only discovers this after reboot, when the machine comes up from the USB again.

problems.title: Dead / inconsistent navigation code: fieldCount() claims 3 rows for stepIdentity and update()'s 'r' branch for stepIdentity is unreachable
problems.why_wrong: update() dispatches stepIdentity to updateIdentity at panel/view_setup.go:166-168 before the generic switch, so `case "r": if s.step == stepIdentity` can never fire. Likewise moveField/fieldCount are never used for stepIdentity (it uses identityRows() = 1 + len(networks) + 1), yet fieldCount hard-codes `case stepIdentity: return 3 // pcName, ssid, pass` — a stale model where the SSID was typed by hand. The s.ssid textinput itself is never focused or rendered (activeTextInput never returns it); it is only a hidden value holder.
problems.failure_scenario: Not user-visible today, but it is a live trap: anyone who later routes stepIdentity through the generic path (or calls moveField on it) gets a 3-row cursor over a list that actually has 1+N+1 rows, immediately producing out-of-range cursor states in updateIdentity/networkAt.

recommendations: panel/view_setup.go:411 — guard the stepInstall branch of advance() with `if s.installSuccess { reboot now }` (or reset s.cursor and route Enter to the reboot path) so the success screen's "Hemen Yeniden Başlat  Enter" button actually reboots instead of re-running mcos-install.

Decide what the disk install means for the wizard: either move stepInstall to the end (after stepConfirm) so doSetupSave runs first and mcos-install can copy a real config.json into MCOS-DATA, or call doSetupSave before doInstallOS. As it stands every setting collected after step 5 is discarded whenever the user installs.

panel/view_setup.go:436 — change back() to `if s.step > stepIntro { s.step--; ... }` (with an explicit rule for stepIdentity/stepInstall if re-entering them is undesirable), or stop rendering the "Geri" action on steps where it is a no-op (panel/view_setup.go:639).

Persist the PC name: add a hostname field to model.Config, set it in buildConfig() from s.pcName, and have the daemon apply it (sethostname + /etc/hostname). Otherwise drop the field and its mandatory validation from the wizard.

panel/view_setup.go:192-197 — do not consume left/right/h/l/space when activeTextInput() != nil. Move the adjust() cases behind a `if s.activeTextInput() == nil` check so the nodeName field can receive ordinary characters and caret movement.

panel/view_setup.go:228 / 873 — make identityRows() and viewIdentity agree: either cap identityRows at 1+min(len(networks),8)+1, or scroll/window the rendered list around the cursor so the selected row is always visible.

panel/messages.go:177 — either implement the dlPlugins pre-download or remove the checkbox; and move the dlJava downloads out of doInstallOS so the option is honoured on the "Atla" path too. Surface JavaInstall errors instead of `_, _ =`.
panel/app.go:151 — handle disksMsg.err (set setup.errMsg, e.g. "disk listesi alınamadı: …") so an RPC failure is not rendered as "no disks found".

panel/view_setup.go:1064 — return the UpdateConfig and Persist failures into the setup model (a dedicated setupErrMsg that sets s.errMsg) rather than errMsg{}, which app.go routes to a.statusErr that View() never renders while a.setup != nil. Also guard against repeated Enter presses firing multiple saves.

panel/view_setup.go:493 — seed buildConfig() from the currently loaded a.config (when one exists) instead of model.DefaultConfig(), so re-running the wizard from Ayarlar does not silently reset Turbo, AutostartServers, WAN, Features and Tier.
panel/view_setup.go:513 — make handleJavaSetup clear only javaDetecting, not s.loading, so a late javaSetupMsg cannot unlock the keyboard during a disk install.

Either implement the documented gate (block/warn on the Java and install steps while `!s.status.Net.Internet || !s.status.ClockSynced`) or delete the s.status field and fix the two comments that claim the gate exists (panel/view_setup.go:63 and internal/daemon/handlers_system.go:236).

Add an explicit confirmation before doInstallOS (a yes/no row or a typed device name), given that Enter is the universal "continue" key everywhere else in the wizard and back() from stepTheme lands on stepInstall with the cursor on the first disk.

surveys.summary: MCOS has no offline install path at all: every server flavour, every mod/plugin, and the JRE itself are fetched live over HTTP at install time, with no on-disk artifact cache, no bundled fallback, and no "offline mode" flag anywhere in the tree. Making offline Fabric 1.21.11 + ViaVersion work requires four separate additions (a local Fabric provider path, a pre-seeded .mcos-launch.json or equivalent, a bundled JRE that gets registered into /data/java/index.json without java.detect being called manually, and a ViaFabric jar in mods/ since installViaVersion hard-skips all non-plugin flavours) plus a decision to put the payload in the MCOS-DATA seed partition rather than the 122 MB initramfs.

facts.claim: The provider contract is a 2-method interface; every flavour must implement Software() and Install(), and Install receives an *http.Client — there is no filesystem/offline parameter.
InstallResult is the only thing persisted about how to launch: JarFile / ArgsFile / Script / LaunchArgs / Notes, all JSON-tagged.
facts.evidence: internal/server/providers/provider.go:21-28 — `type InstallResult struct { JarFile string `json:"jarFile,omitempty"`; ArgsFile ...; Script ...; LaunchArgs []string `json:"launchArgs,omitempty"`; Notes ... }`

facts.claim: Providers are registered in a package-level map by an init() function; there is no way to inject or override a provider from outside the package.
facts.evidence: internal/server/providers/provider.go:41-43 `var registry = map[model.Software]Provider{}` / `func register(p Provider)` / `func Get(s model.Software) (Provider, bool)`, populated in `func init()` at provider.go:50-61.

facts.claim: All provider downloads funnel through exactly two unexported helpers, both plain HTTP GETs with no cache, no retry, and no local-file fallback.
facts.evidence: internal/server/providers/provider.go:66 `func getJSON(ctx, client, url, v any) error` and provider.go:83 `func downloadTo(ctx, client, url, dir, filename string) (string, error)`; both build `http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, url, nil)` and error out on any non-200.

problems.title: No offline path exists at any layer — install is a hard network dependency with no fallback
problems.why_wrong: getJSON and downloadTo are the only ways any provider obtains bytes. Both do a bare http GET and return an error on connection failure. There is no cache lookup, no local-file probe, no bundled-artifact directory, and the Provider interface has no parameter through which one could be supplied.
problems.failure_scenario: Box boots with no uplink -> user creates a Fabric 1.21.x server -> handlers.go:410 java.Install fails first with `java 21 indirme hatası: download: dial tcp: no such host`; if a JDK were somehow present, fabric.go:30 then fails with `fabric: loaders for "1.21.11": Get "https://meta.fabricmc.net/v2/versions/loader/1.21.11": dial tcp ...`. Server never installs, never starts.

problems.title: Bundling server.jar alone is not sufficient for Fabric — the launcher fetches its libraries at first RUN
problems.why_wrong: MCOS downloads Fabric's server *launcher* jar, not a fully materialised server. The code's own comment states it "resolves the rest of its libraries on first run". Those runtime fetches (vanilla server jar, fabric-loader, intermediary, mixin/ASM) go out over the network from inside the JVM, where MCOS has no visibility or control, and are not recorded in .mcos-launch.json.
problems.failure_scenario: A bundle ships server.jar and a hand-written .mcos-launch.json, so EnsureInstalled is skipped and Start succeeds in spawning `java -jar server.jar nogui`. The JVM then tries to download the 1.21.x server jar and loader libs, fails offline, and exits non-zero. onExit (manager.go:411) flips the state to Error with `[MCOS HATA] Sunucu süreci beklenmeyen bir şekilde durdu` and the user sees no actionable cause.

problems.title: The only Java offline hook (/opt/mcos/java) is never triggered automatically, so a bundled JRE would sit unused
problems.why_wrong: candidateDirs() includes /opt/mcos/java, which is clearly the intended bundle location, but Detect() runs only from the java.detect RPC (handlers_java.go:56). Nothing calls it at daemon startup, and panel/client.go:161's JavaDetect wrapper has zero callers in the panel. Meanwhile handlers.go:405 decides whether Java is present purely by reading the index (java.List()), which a never-run Detect never populates.
problems.failure_scenario: Image ships a JRE at /opt/mcos/java/temurin-21/bin/java. User creates a server. handlers.go:405 iterates java.List() -> index.json is empty -> handlers.go:410 calls java.Install(21) -> Adoptium download fails offline -> CodeConflict error. The perfectly good bundled JRE 30 cm away on disk is never looked at.

problems.title: ViaVersion is unreachable for Fabric by design — the requested feature combination is not implementable with the current compat code
problems.why_wrong: installViaVersion returns immediately when !srv.SupportsPlugins, and model.go:35-41 excludes Fabric from SupportsPlugins(). So even ONLINE, ticking AllowOldVersions on a Fabric server installs nothing; it only logs "ViaVersion not applicable". The user's stated goal (Fabric + ViaVersion preinstalled) has no code path at all, offline or online.
problems.failure_scenario: User creates Fabric 1.21.x with AllowOldVersions=true. install.go:95 calls installViaVersion, which logs the not-applicable line and returns. No jar lands in mods/ or plugins/. A 1.20 client connects and is rejected with a protocol-version mismatch.

problems.title: Bundling into the initramfs would roughly double or triple both image size and boot RAM footprint
problems.why_wrong: BR2_TARGET_ROOTFS_CPIO + _GZIP means the whole rootfs is a gzip cpio that the kernel unpacks into tmpfs at boot. The measured cost today is 122 MB compressed / 269 MB resident. JDK/JRE + MC server jar + loader libs + Via jar are all already-compressed or poorly-compressible content, so they add close to their raw size to rootfs.cpio.gz and their full size to RAM.
problems.failure_scenario: Adding a full Temurin 21 JDK (what temurinURL fetches today — note it requests /jdk/, not a JRE) plus a 1.21.x server jar to the overlay pushes rootfs.cpio.gz past ~350 MB and the resident tmpfs past ~500 MB. On a 1 GB target the kernel OOMs during initramfs unpack, or boots with too little RAM left for a Minecraft server that wants 1-2 GB heap. mkusb.sh:30 BOOT_MB=768 (sized for a ~122 MB initrd) also becomes too small and mkusb.sh:111 dies with "boot bölümü küçük".

problems.title: Offline, the panel cannot even offer the target version — 1.21.11 is not in the fallback list
problems.why_wrong: When the Mojang manifest is unreachable, handleServerVersions returns the hardcoded fallbackVersions slice, whose newest entry is 1.21.4. The in-memory verCache is not persisted, so even a machine that was once online offers the fallback list after a reboot.
problems.failure_scenario: Offline box, user opens the create-server wizard (panel/messages.go:204 -> cl.ServerVersions). The version picker lists 1.21.4 at newest. The user cannot select 1.21.11 at all, so the bundled artifacts would never be requested even if everything else worked.

problems.title: Nothing seeds /data, and rootfs content at /data is masked by the persistent mount
problems.why_wrong: The seed directory that becomes the MCOS-DATA ext4 partition contains only three empty dirs (servers/, java/, log/). Meanwhile post-build.sh:56 creates /data in the rootfs, but S99mcos:17 mount_persistent() mounts MCOS-DATA on top of it, so any file the initramfs placed at /data becomes invisible the moment the partition is found.
problems.failure_scenario: A developer bundles a JRE by dropping it into rootfs-overlay/data/java/. On a USB-installed box the MCOS-DATA partition mounts over /data and the JRE vanishes; on a box where mcos-findfs fails, /data stays in RAM and the JRE works — so the bundle appears to work in QEMU and silently disappears on real hardware.

recommendations: Do NOT put the payload in the initramfs. Put it in the MCOS-DATA seed: extend scripts/mkusb.sh:206-212 so $SEED is populated from a new bundle/ directory before mke2fs -d runs. That costs zero initramfs bytes, zero boot RAM, survives install via mcos-install:314's `cp -a /data/. \"$TARGET_MNT/\"`, and needs no Buildroot change. The only case it does not cover is a pure-ISO boot (Makefile iso: ships only bzImage + initrd.img), which has no data partition at all.

Seed Java as a ready-registered runtime, not as files to be discovered: place the JRE at /data/java/temurin-21/ in the seed AND write /data/java/index.json containing a model.JavaRuntime with Major:21, Vendor:"temurin", Path:"/data/java/temurin-21", JavaBin:"/data/java/temurin-21/bin/java". That satisfies java.Manager.Get -> Ensure (manager.go:100) and handlers.go:405's java.List() check with no code change at all. If you instead bundle to /opt/mcos/java (inside the initramfs), you MUST also add a `d.java.Detect()` call to daemon startup — today detect.go:114's /opt/mcos/java entry is dead code because Detect() only runs from the java.detect RPC.

Ship a headless jlink'd JRE 21, not the JDK. temurinURL (download.go:37-43) currently requests `/jdk/`; a full JDK is several times the size of a `jlink --add-modules java.base,java.logging,java.management,java.naming,java.desktop,jdk.unsupported --strip-debug --no-header-files --no-man-pages` image, which is what a Minecraft server actually needs. Verify the resulting bin/java runs against the glibc toolchain in mcos_defconfig (BR2_TOOLCHAIN_BUILDROOT_GLIBC) — a distro JRE built against a newer glibc will not start on this rootfs.

For Fabric, bundling server.jar is NOT enough. Either (a) run the Fabric server launcher once at image-build time inside a prepared server directory and bundle the whole resulting tree (server.jar + the .fabric/ library cache + the vanilla server jar + libraries/), or (b) add a new provider path that lays out a fully-materialised server dir. Option (a) is far cheaper and needs no Go change, because install.go's launchInfo is just JSON — see the next item.

Seed the whole server directory plus its .mcos-launch.json so the provider is never invoked. Write /data/servers/<id>/data/.mcos-launch.json containing {"jarFile":"server.jar","launchArgs":["nogui"],"installed":true}; IsInstalled (install.go:30) then returns true and EnsureInstalled (manager.go:269) short-circuits before any network call. You must also seed the matching /data/servers/<id>/server.json manifest so store.GetServer finds it, plus eula.txt and server.properties (install.go:159-200 normally writes these).

ViaVersion cannot work on Fabric — bundle ViaFabric (or ViaFabricPlus) into <serverData>/mods/ instead. compat.go:16's `if !srv.SupportsPlugins { return }` guard means Fabric is skipped unconditionally; compat.go:13-14 says so explicitly. If you want MCOS to handle this itself rather than via a seeded directory, extend installViaVersion with a SupportsMods branch that calls catalog.InstallByID with slug "viafabric" and destDir filepath.Join(dataDir, "mods") — mirroring contentDirFor in handlers_catalog.go:31-40.

Add 1.21.11 (or whatever the bundled version is) to fallbackVersions in internal/daemon/handlers_net.go:88, and ideally persist the successful Mojang fetch to disk instead of the in-memory verCache (handlers_net.go:93-99) so a once-online box keeps a real list across reboots. Without this the offline wizard cannot even offer the bundled version.

Add an explicit offline/local-artifact lookup rather than relying on pre-seeded launch files: give providers.downloadTo (provider.go:83) a check for a local cache dir (e.g. /opt/mcos/artifacts/<sha or filename>) before the HTTP GET, and give catalog.DownloadTo (catalog.go:178) the same. This is a small, contained change that makes every flavour and every mod bundleable, instead of special-casing Fabric.

If you do choose the initramfs route, copy the nerd-font pattern exactly: a new os/buildroot/external/package/mcos-java/ with *_SITE pointing at a local directory, *_SITE_METHOD = local, and *_INSTALL_TARGET_CMDS copying into $(TARGET_DIR)/opt/mcos/java/, plus a Config.in sourced from external/Config.in and a BR2_PACKAGE_MCOS_JAVA=y line in mcos_defconfig. external.mk already globs package/*/*.mk so no wiring beyond that is needed. Also bump mkusb.sh:30 BOOT_MB (currently 768, sized for a ~122 MB initrd) or mkusb.sh:111 will abort.

Alternative worth evaluating before hand-rolling: os/buildroot/buildroot/package/openjdk and openjdk-bin already exist in this checkout and are simply not enabled in mcos_defconfig. Enabling BR2_PACKAGE_OPENJDK* would give a cross-built JVM in the rootfs at a standard prefix — but it lands in the initramfs (same size problem) and detect.go's candidateDirs would need to cover wherever Buildroot installs it.
