problems.title: fbfont.Face documents itself as concurrency-safe but has a genuine data race
problems.location: internal/fbfont/font.go:44 (false claim) and font.go:157 (rasterise called outside the lock)
problems.why_wrong: The doc says 'Eşzamanlı kullanım güvenlidir: Glyph() önbelleğini kendi kilidiyle korur.' The RWMutex protects only the map. Glyph() releases the read lock, then calls rasterise(), which touches the SHARED font.Face via GlyphBounds() and font.Drawer.DrawString(). opentype.Face wraps a single sfnt.Buffer that LoadGlyph mutates, so two goroutines rasterising different runes corrupt each other's state.
problems.failure_scenario: A render goroutine drawing a frame while a prefetch/warm-up goroutine primes the cache: both call Glyph() for uncached runes, both enter rasterise(), and sfnt.(*Font).LoadGlyph races on its shared buffer -> corrupted or wrong glyph masks, or a panic. I reproduced the exact pattern outside the repo (shared opentype.Face, cache guarded by RWMutex, rasterise outside it) and Go's race detector reported: 'WARNING: DATA RACE / Read at 0x00c000139568 by goroutine 10: golang.org/x/image/font/sfnt.(*Font).LoadGlyph() sfnt.go:1439 ... Previous write at 0x00c000139568 by goroutine 16: ... LoadGlyph() sfnt.go:1439'. The package's own tests are single-goroutine so they never surface it.

problems.title: GRUB caps the framebuffer at 1024x768 — the 1920x1080 goal is unreachable today
problems.why_wrong: `set gfxmode=1024x768,800x600,auto` lists 1024x768 first and never mentions any 1080p mode. With `set gfxpayload=keep` (:247) the kernel simply inherits whatever GRUB selected, and since no native KMS driver is built in, nothing can change it afterwards.
problems.failure_scenario: On a 1080p monitor the appliance boots, GRUB picks 1024x768, efifb/simpledrm hands the kernel a 1024x768 surface, and the new framebuffer UI renders at 1024x768 stretched/letterboxed by the display. fbfont.Grid(1024,768) at 16px yields 102x38 cells instead of the 192x54 the design assumes.

problems.title: No VT takeover: fbcon will repaint over anything drawn to /dev/fb0
problems.location: os/buildroot/external/board/mcos/rootfs-overlay/usr/bin/mcos-launch (whole file) — no KDSETMODE anywhere in the repo
problems.why_wrong: CONFIG_FRAMEBUFFER_CONSOLE=y means fbcon owns the console and keeps drawing (cursor blink, kernel messages, echoed keystrokes) into the same memory a pixel renderer writes. Nothing in the tree puts the VT into KD_GRAPHICS or unbinds fbcon. Today this is masked because fbterm does that work; removing fbterm removes the protection.
problems.failure_scenario: mcos-panel opens /dev/fb0 and draws a frame; the console cursor blinks a character cell into the middle of a rounded card, a printk at loglevel<=4 scrolls the whole screen, and every keypress echoes as text over the UI. `grep -rn 'KDSETMODE|KD_GRAPHICS|VT_ACTIVATE|KDGETMODE' cmd/ internal/ panel/ os/buildroot/external/` returns nothing.

problems.title: No keyboard input path exists for a framebuffer UI
problems.why_wrong: The panel is keyboard-only and currently receives keys through Bubble Tea reading the tty's stdin, which fbterm provides. A renderer that draws pixels directly and puts the VT in graphics mode must source key events itself (evdev, or raw/K_MEDIUMRAW tty mode), and no such code exists anywhere in the Go tree.
problems.failure_scenario: The framebuffer panel renders a perfect first frame and then accepts no input at all — arrow keys and Enter do nothing, because nothing is reading /dev/input/event* and the tty is no longer in a cooked line mode Bubble Tea understands. `grep -rn '/dev/input|evdev|EVIOCG|linux/input' --include=*.go cmd/ internal/ panel/` returns nothing.

problems.title: No mode setting anywhere: fbdev cannot change resolution and no KMS driver could honour it
problems.why_wrong: Only the two GET ioctls are declared (fbioGetVScreenInfo 0x4600, fbioGetFScreenInfo 0x4602). FBIOPUT_VSCREENINFO (0x4601) is absent, so Device can only accept the mode it is handed. Combined with I915/AMDGPU/NOUVEAU/RADEON all being '# not set' in the built .config, there is no layer in the stack that can select 1920x1080 on real hardware.
problems.failure_scenario: Someone fixes the GRUB gfxmode line but the firmware's GOP does not offer 1080p (common on BIOS/VESA, which typically tops out at 1024x768 or 1280x1024). There is no fallback: the Go code cannot request a mode, and no KMS driver exists to set one, so the appliance is stuck at whatever the firmware chose.

problems.title: Device.Flip never sets the alpha/transparency channel at 32bpp
problems.why_wrong: The packed value is built from only the R/G/B shifts (`v := ...Red<<rShift | Green<<gShift | Blue<<bShift`) and then `d.mem[o+3] = byte(v >> 24)` writes the top byte. The fb_var_screeninfo Transp bitfield is parsed into the struct but never read — `grep -rn 'Transp' internal/fbdev/` matches only the struct field declaration (device_linux.go:37) and a test offset assertion. On an XRGB8888 surface the byte is ignored, but on a surface reporting transp.length=8 (ARGB8888) this writes alpha 0.
problems.failure_scenario: A driver or firmware handoff that reports transp.offset=24/transp.length=8 gets a fully transparent (or black, depending on the compositor path) screen even though every RGB value is correct — a silent, very hard-to-diagnose blank display.

problems.title: 13 codepoints the panel renders are absent from the embedded font, with no fallback
problems.why_wrong: fbfont embeds exactly one face and has no fallback chain; Glyph() returns Missing=true and the caller is expected to draw a placeholder. The panel currently emits ↻ ⌁ ▸ ◂ ◈ ◍ ★ ⚑ ⚙ ⚠ ✗ ✦ ℹ, none of which the TTF contains. fbdraw exists precisely to replace these, but the token definitions still reference the characters.
problems.failure_scenario: Porting the panel as-is to the framebuffer renderer leaves 13 glyphs rendering as tofu/placeholder boxes — including ⚠ (used 4x in app.go) and ◈ (6x in tokens.go). This is the same class of bug the fbterm font-fallback chain caused, just relocated.

problems.title: The recovery boot entry disables the framebuffer entirely
problems.why_wrong: The recovery menuentry sets `gfxpayload=text` and passes `nomodeset vga=normal`. That yields an 80x25 VGA text console with no /dev/fb0 at all. Once the UI is pure framebuffer drawing, recovery mode has no UI.
problems.failure_scenario: A user boots recovery to diagnose a problem; fbdev.Open('/dev/fb0') fails with 'fbdev: /dev/fb0 açılamadı', and the graphical panel cannot start — so the mode intended for troubleshooting is the one mode with no interface.

problems.title: CONFIG_FB_SIMPLE=y in kernel.config is dead configuration
problems.why_wrong: The comment above it claims it is needed for 'BIOS/UEFI VM compatibility', but FB_SIMPLE is mutually exclusive with DRM_SIMPLEDRM, which is enabled at line 87. The built config confirms the option was silently dropped.
problems.failure_scenario: Not a runtime failure, but actively misleading: anyone debugging a missing framebuffer will read line 216, believe simplefb is active, and look in the wrong place. Evidence: `grep -E '^(CONFIG_FB_SIMPLE=|# CONFIG_FB_SIMPLE is not set)' output/build/linux-6.6.32/.config` -> '<absent from .config>'; and linux-6.6.32/drivers/video/fbdev/Kconfig shows 'config FB_SIMPLE / tristate "Simple framebuffer support" / depends on FB / depends on !DRM_SIMPLEDRM'.

problems.title: go.mod marks directly-imported modules as indirect
problems.location: go.mod (require block, 'golang.org/x/image v0.46.0 // indirect' and 'golang.org/x/sys v0.48.0 // indirect')
problems.why_wrong: internal/fbfont imports golang.org/x/image/font, .../font/opentype and .../math/fixed; internal/fbdraw imports golang.org/x/image/vector; internal/fbdev imports golang.org/x/sys/unix. All are direct dependencies but are still tagged // indirect, meaning the new packages were added without a `go mod tidy`.
problems.failure_scenario: A future `go mod tidy` silently rewrites go.mod (promoting both to direct), producing unrelated diff noise in a commit; and until then the module graph misrepresents what the project actually depends on.

problems.title: fbdev's rendering hot path and canvas helpers are untested
problems.location: internal/fbdev/device_linux_test.go (only 2 tests) and internal/fbdev/canvas.go (no test file)
problems.why_wrong: Flip() is the one function that converts pixels for real hardware — it contains the stride arithmetic, the 16/24/32bpp branches and scale8() — and nothing exercises it. canvas.go (NewCanvas, Fill, SavePNG) has no test file at all. By contrast fbdraw has 12 pixel-level tests and fbfont has 8, so the weakest-tested package is the one closest to the hardware.
problems.failure_scenario: A stride or channel-shift regression in Flip (e.g. swapping rShift/bShift, or using xres instead of LineLength) produces a skewed or colour-swapped screen that only appears on real hardware, with a green test suite. Flip cannot be tested against /dev/fb0 in CI, but it can be tested by injecting a fake mem slice + vinf/finf.

recommendations: Port strategy — do NOT write an ANSI parser. The decisive fact is that panel/app.go:634 View() returns the whole UI as one string, so an fbui layer can call a.View() directly and never involve a terminal. But fbdraw's entire reason for existing (painter.go:1-26) is that box-drawing characters cannot produce single-piece rounded corners. Parsing View()'s output would faithfully reproduce the character-cell look the user explicitly wants to get rid of. Treat an ANSI parser only as a throwaway bring-up scaffold, if at all.

If a bring-up scaffold IS wanted, it is genuinely cheap: under the pinned termenv.ANSI profile lipgloss emits only ESC[<params>m with params drawn from {0,1,2,3,4,5,7,9,53} u {30-37,90-97} u {40-47,100-107} — no 38;5 and no 38;2 forms — and every styled run self-terminates with ESC[0m, so no attribute stack is needed. That is roughly a 60-line SGR parser. It stays valid even under TrueColor as long as the theme keeps addressing colours by numeric slot ('0'-'7', panel/theme/palette.go:44-53).

Fix the resolution chain before any renderer work, in this order: (1) change mcos-install:243 to `set gfxmode=1920x1080,1600x900,1366x768,1024x768,auto`; (2) keep gfxpayload=keep; (3) accept that without a native KMS driver the mode is fixed at boot. If real 1080p on Intel/AMD hardware is a hard requirement, enable CONFIG_DRM_I915/CONFIG_DRM_AMDGPU (currently '# not set') and budget for the firmware blobs and kernel size that brings.

Add VT takeover before drawing a single pixel in production: ioctl KDSETMODE/KD_GRAPHICS on the panel VT (and KD_TEXT on exit, including on signal), or unbind fbcon via /sys/class/vtconsole/vtcon*/bind — CONFIG_VT_HW_CONSOLE_BINDING=y is already enabled in the built kernel, so the sysfs route is available. Also keep the existing `echo 0 > /proc/sys/kernel/printk` from mcos-launch:36.

Design the input path now, as it is a peer of the renderer, not an afterthought: read /dev/input/event* (evdev) and translate to the key events panel/app.go already handles, or put the tty in raw/K_MEDIUMRAW mode. Nothing in the tree reads input today outside Bubble Tea's stdin reader.

Fix the fbfont concurrency claim one of two ways: either hold a plain sync.Mutex across rasterise() (simplest, and fine because glyphs are cached after first use), or delete the 'Eşzamanlı kullanım güvenlidir' sentence at font.go:44 and document Face as single-goroutine. Do not leave a false safety claim in place. Add a -race test that calls Glyph() from several goroutines.

Use the Transp bitfield in Flip, or explicitly document why it is ignored: at 32bpp set the transparency bits to full opacity when d.vinf.Transp.Length > 0 instead of writing byte(v>>24), which is currently always 0 for standard XRGB layouts.

Add tests for the one untested hardware-facing function: Flip() can be tested without /dev/fb0 by making Device's mem/vinf/finf injectable, then asserting exact byte output for XRGB8888, BGRX8888, RGB565 and a padded stride. canvas.go needs a test file too.

Reconcile panel/theme/tokens.go with the fbdraw contract: the 13 codepoints that are missing from the embedded font (↻ ⌁ ▸ ◂ ◈ ◍ ★ ⚑ ⚙ ⚠ ✗ ✦ ℹ) should become fbdraw shape calls, and the token constants should stop naming characters that cannot be drawn. Also replace the runtime strings.Repeat("─"/"█") sites (app.go:851, components.go:362-363,403, view_detail.go:674, view_misc.go:67-68, view_setup.go:712-713) with fbdraw.HLine / FillRoundRect.

Delete or correct kernel.config:216 (CONFIG_FB_SIMPLE=y) and its comment — it is silently dropped because FB_SIMPLE depends on !DRM_SIMPLEDRM, and DRM_SIMPLEDRM=y at line 87 already provides the same capability through DRM_FBDEV_EMULATION.

Give the recovery boot entry (mcos-install:252-254) a usable UI, or accept it as a serial/text-only shell. As written, `nomodeset vga=normal` leaves no /dev/fb0, so the graphical panel cannot run in the exact mode meant for troubleshooting.
Run `go mod tidy` so golang.org/x/image v0.46.0 and golang.org/x/sys v0.48.0 are recorded as direct requirements, since fbfont/fbdraw/fbdev import them directly.

Scope note for planning: the port surface is ~7,028 non-test lines across panel/ + panel/theme/, but the lipgloss feature surface a custom renderer must reproduce is small and well-bounded — RoundedBorder is the ONLY border style used, there are just 3 Place sites and 13 Join sites, and Align/MaxWidth/Margin/Italic/Underline/Inline are used nowhere. The real work is layout and content, not exotic lipgloss features.

critical_findings.finding: A complete vector widget layer already exists and is wired to the drawing primitives: internal/fbui/widgets.go imports mcos/internal/fbdraw and mcos/internal/fbfont and provides Panel, Button, ButtonRow, Radio, Check, Chevron, Row, Divider, Progress, StatusDot, Badge, Text/TextCenter/TextRight — all single-piece vector shapes, no box-drawing characters. internal/fbui/mockup_test.go renders four full-screen PNGs (01-secim-ekrani, 02-kurulum-disk, 03-ana-ekran, 04-ekran-ayarlari) at 1280x800 with an 18px face.
critical_findings.implication: Do NOT start a new renderer and do NOT write an ANSI parser over panel/app.go View(). The request-1 work is: bridge fbui to fbdev, then reimplement each panel screen as a Draw(u *fbui.UI) function. The existing mockups are the visual contract and the PNG harness is the automated verification mechanism — extend it, do not replace it.

critical_findings.finding: The blockers for a pixel UI are not drawing — they are VT ownership and input. grep for KDSETMODE|KD_GRAPHICS|/dev/input|vtcon across cmd/ internal/ panel/ returns nothing. fbcon is compiled in (CONFIG_FRAMEBUFFER_CONSOLE=y) and today fbterm is the only thing keeping the console off the framebuffer; mcos-launch runs the panel inside fbterm on tty2.
critical_findings.implication: Two new packages are mandatory before any pixel is drawn in production: a VT-takeover package (KDSETMODE/KD_GRAPHICS with restore on exit and signals, CONFIG_VT_HW_CONSOLE_BINDING=y is available as the sysfs alternative) and an evdev input package feeding the existing Bubble Tea key handling. Removing fbterm without both produces a UI that is overwritten by the console cursor and accepts no keystrokes.

critical_findings.finding: The UEFI kernel-panic root cause is ALREADY FIXED in the uncommitted working tree. mcos-install now writes BOOTX64.EFI only from $BOOTLIB/BOOTX64.EFI (line 269, the grub-mkimage output), the kernel goes only to /boot/boot/bzImage (line 226), and startup.nsh appears nowhere in the repo. The EFISTUB block still exists at git HEAD.
critical_findings.implication: Request 4 is not 'fix the panic', it is 'lock the fix in before it regresses and harden the surrounding path'. This must be the first commit: the fix currently lives only in an uncommitted working tree and no test can detect its removal.

critical_findings.finding: Nothing can detect a regression of that exact fix. test-install-logic.sh passes today and never mentions BOOTX64, EFI/BOOT, startup.nsh or the GRUB prefix; verify-usb.sh only greps a recursive FAT listing for a name matching 'BOOTX64' and for 'grub *cfg' at any path; and an MZ magic check cannot distinguish a raw bzImage from a GRUB EFI image (both start with MZ, measured).
critical_findings.implication: Add explicit assertions in scripts/test-install-logic.sh: zero lines copying $KERNEL/bzImage to BOOTX64.EFI, zero occurrences of startup.nsh, and a cross-check that the grub.cfg destination path in mcos-install equals the -p prefix in post-build.sh. This is the cheapest high-value step in the whole plan.

critical_findings.finding: Resolution is a bootloader-only property on this system. mcos-install:243 sets gfxmode=1024x768,800x600,auto with gfxpayload=keep; the kernel has no native KMS driver (I915/AMDGPU/RADEON/NOUVEAU/AST/MGAG200 all '# not set' in the built 6.6.32 .config), only efifb/vesafb/simpledrm handoff; internal/fbdev declares only FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO (0x4600) and FBIOGET_FSCREENINFO (0x4602) — FBIOPUT_VSCREENINFO is absent.
critical_findings.implication: Request 2 splits in two: raising resolution is a one-line grub.cfg change replicated in three places (mcos-install:243, Makefile:179, scripts/mkusb.sh:159, which currently disagree). The display-settings screen cannot mode-set at runtime; it must rewrite grub.cfg and require a reboot. Its 'Uygula' button must be labelled as reboot-required.

critical_findings.finding: The FAT boot/ESP partition is never mounted at runtime: etc/fstab has no /boot entry and S99mcos mount_persistent() mounts only MCOS-DATA at /data.
critical_findings.implication: The display-settings screen must itself locate the boot partition (/usr/bin/mcos-findfs MCOS-BOOT), mount it, rewrite BOTH /boot/grub/grub.cfg and /EFI/BOOT/grub.cfg, sync and unmount. That is privileged filesystem work in the daemon, not the panel — it needs a new IPC method, not a UI-only change.

critical_findings.finding: Confirmed by reading panel/view_setup.go:411-416: the stepInstall branch of advance() has no installSuccess guard, while installSuccess is set at :527 and only read at :664 for rendering. After a successful install the cursor still points at the installed disk, so the 'Hemen Yeniden Başlat  Enter' button re-runs doInstallOS on the disk that was just installed.
critical_findings.implication: Request 5 has a concrete, reproducible data-loss bug at the top of the list. Fix it with an explicit installSuccess branch that reboots, and add a panel unit test that drives the model to installDoneMsg and asserts Enter does not emit doInstallOS.

critical_findings.finding: The disk install happens at step 5 of 10 and hard-reboots on success, so stepTheme/Budget/Cluster/FirstServer/Confirm never run — and doSetupSave (the only caller of UpdateConfig) runs exclusively from stepConfirm. Meanwhile mcos-install:305-325 does 'cp -a /data/. $TARGET_MNT/' on the assumption that OOBE settings already exist in /data as config.json.
critical_findings.implication: The wizard's step order is structurally wrong and must be reordered as part of the rewrite: either move stepInstall after stepConfirm, or call doSetupSave before doInstallOS. Without this, every setting the user enters is discarded on the install path and the installed machine reruns the full wizard.

critical_findings.finding: Fabric offline needs four separate things, not one. (a) internal/server/providers/fabric.go makes three live HTTP calls and its own comment at :47-48 admits the downloaded launcher 'resolves the rest of its libraries on first run' — bundling server.jar alone still fails at server START. (b) internal/server/compat.go:16 returns immediately for any flavour where !SupportsPlugins, and Fabric is excluded from SupportsPlugins, so ViaVersion is never installed for Fabric even online. (c) Java comes only from Adoptium over HTTPS. (d) internal/daemon/handlers.go:400-413 calls java.Install() synchronously and hard-errors before the server package is reached.
critical_findings.implication: Request 3 requires a pre-materialised server directory (run the Fabric launcher once at build time and capture the whole tree including .fabric/ and libraries/), a ViaFabric jar dropped in mods/ (not plugins/), a jlink'd JRE registered in /data/java/index.json, and a seeded .mcos-launch.json + server.json so EnsureInstalled short-circuits. No single-point fix exists.

critical_findings.finding: The correct delivery vehicle already exists and is empty: scripts/mkusb.sh:207-213 builds the MCOS-DATA ext4 partition from $SEED with mke2fs -d (currently just empty servers/, java/, log/ dirs), and mcos-install:312-314 does 'cp -a /data/.' so anything seeded survives the permanent install. The initramfs is the wrong place: rootfs.cpio.gz is 122 MB compressed / 269 MB resident, and anything added costs both image size and boot RAM. Baking into rootfs /data is useless because S99mcos mounts MCOS-DATA over it.
critical_findings.implication: Put the entire offline bundle in the MCOS-DATA seed. Zero Buildroot changes, zero initramfs growth. The one case it does not cover is the pure-ISO boot path (Makefile iso: ships only bzImage + initrd.img, no data partition) — that must be documented as 'offline bundle requires the USB/installed image'.

critical_findings.finding: The built Buildroot output tree is stale: os/buildroot/output/target/usr/lib/mcos does not exist and rootfs.cpio.gz contains zero usr/lib/mcos entries, so mcos-install would abort at its own guard with 'önyükleyici dosyaları imajda yok'.
critical_findings.implication: A full rebuild is a hard prerequisite for any boot/QEMU verification step. Schedule it before the first end-to-end test, not after.

critical_findings.finding: internal/fbfont/font.go claims concurrency safety at :44 but releases the RWMutex before calling rasterise() at :157, which touches the shared opentype.Face / sfnt.Buffer. The ui survey reproduced the exact race outside the repo with the race detector.
critical_findings.implication: Fix before the render loop grows a second goroutine (prefetch, async redraw). A sync.Mutex held across rasterise costs nothing since glyphs are cached after first use. Add a -race test calling Glyph() from several goroutines.

contradictions: FALSE CLAIM in the ui survey: 'Nothing in cmd/, panel/ or the rest of internal/ imports fbdev, fbfont or fbdraw — the groundwork is entirely unwired.' I verified internal/fbui/widgets.go:8-9 imports both mcos/internal/fbdraw and mcos/internal/fbfont, and internal/fbui/mockup_test.go imports them too. The ui survey enumerated three packages (fbdev/fbfont/fbdraw) and missed the fourth and most important one — fbui, 480 non-test lines plus a 387-line mockup harness. The boot survey did find fbui. Consequence: the ui survey's scope estimate ('~7,028 non-test lines would be affected by a port') and its port-strategy discussion are both anchored on a false premise that no widget layer exists. The real gap is narrower: fbui has no fbdev binding, no VT takeover and no input source.

RESOLUTION TARGET conflict: the ui survey recommends 'set gfxmode=1920x1080,1600x900,...' first, but every existing fbui mockup is authored at exactly 1280x800 with an 18px face (verified: four `const W, H = 1280, 800` / `newScreen(t, W, H, 18)` sites). Picking 1080p as the first mode means the mockups' hand-placed panel sizes (760x470, 880x560) no longer match the screen they were designed for. Also, the boot survey notes BIOS/VESA typically tops out near 1024x768-1280x1024, so 1080p is not reliably obtainable. Decide explicitly: target 1280x800/1280x1024 as the design resolution and make fbui.MetricsFor scale layout from the actual fb size, rather than hardcoding a 1080p assumption into either the grub.cfg or the layout code.

THREE-WAY gfxmode disagreement that both surveys noticed but neither resolved: mcos-install:243 = '1024x768,800x600,auto', Makefile:179 = '1024x768,800x600,auto', scripts/mkusb.sh:159 = 'auto', scripts/mkiso.sh:29 = 'auto' plus a kernel 'video=1024x768' at :33. The same machine therefore gets a different resolution from a mkusb image than from an installed disk. mkiso.sh is dead (referenced by nothing) yet is the only file carrying a video= parameter, which will mislead anyone grepping for the resolution knob. One policy, applied to all live sites, and delete or wire up mkiso.sh.

MISLEADING SOURCE COMMENT, confirmed by reading it: internal/server/providers/fabric.go:47-48 says 'Fabric serves a self-contained server launcher jar that resolves the rest of its libraries on first run'. 'Self-contained' and 'resolves the rest of its libraries on first run' are contradictory in the same sentence, and the second half is the operative fact. Anyone planning the offline bundle from this comment will bundle server.jar, see IsInstalled return true, and discover the failure only when the JVM dies offline — surfacing as the generic onExit message 'süreç beklenmeyen bir şekilde durdu'. Rewrite the comment as part of the offline work.

TERMINOLOGY/FEASIBILITY gap in the user request itself: 'Fabric 1.21.11 with ViaVersion preinstalled'. ViaVersion in its plugin form cannot run on Fabric — compat.go:13-14 says so and compat.go:16's `if !srv.SupportsPlugins { return }` enforces it. The Fabric deliverable is ViaFabric (which bundles ViaVersion/ViaBackwards) installed into <serverData>/mods/, not plugins/. Confirm with the user that ViaFabric satisfies the intent before building the bundle.

UNVERIFIABLE VERSION: I could not confirm that Minecraft 1.21.11 exists (no network access from this environment). The daemon's offline fallback list tops out at 1.21.4 (internal/daemon/handlers_net.go:88-91, verified). Pin the exact bundled version at bundle-build time from what the Fabric meta API actually returns, then add that exact string to fallbackVersions — otherwise the offline version picker cannot even offer the version that was bundled, and the whole bundle is unreachable through the UI.

The boot survey states the recovery GRUB entry 'can never display the TUI panel' (gfxpayload=text + nomodeset => no /dev/fb0), and the ui survey independently agrees. This gets strictly worse once the UI is pure framebuffer drawing: today recovery at least reaches show_recovery() in mcos-launch; after the port, the mode intended for troubleshooting is the only mode with no interface at all. Note also that the user's word 'recovery' in request 3 means offline server creation, not this GRUB entry — do not conflate them, but do decide what the GRUB recovery entry becomes (serial/text shell is an acceptable answer, but it must be a decision, not an accident).

The boot survey lists CONFIG_FB_SIMPLE=y in kernel.config:216 as enabled, while the ui survey verified against the BUILT .config that FB_SIMPLE is absent because it depends on !DRM_SIMPLEDRM and DRM_SIMPLEDRM=y at line 87. The ui survey is right; kernel.config:216 and its comment are dead, misleading configuration. Low stakes, but delete it while touching the kernel config so nobody debugs a missing framebuffer from a false lead.

The oobe survey says the Java step is not a dead end offline (verified: viewJava always advances), while quoting code comments at panel/view_setup.go:63 and internal/daemon/handlers_system.go:236 that claim the OOBE gates Java behind internet + ClockSynced. The gate does not exist — s.status is written once at panel/app.go:129 and read nowhere, and a hardcoded time.Sleep(2*time.Second) stands in for NTP. Either implement the gate or delete the field and both comments; leaving the comments is how the next person plans around a feature that is not there.

This must land before UI layout work so the renderer is developed against the resolution it will actually get.

Keep a descending list ending in 'auto' and make the UI layout resolution-independent (step 9) rather than betting on one mode. Verified by: booting UEFI and BIOS and reading /sys/class/graphics/fb0/virtual_size.

Fix verify-usb.sh in this step (derive mode from what is on the FAT partition, use path-exact mdir lookups, and validate BOOTX64.EFI with grub-file --is-x86_64-efi rather than MZ magic) or its output is worse than useless.

ordered_plan.rationale: font.go:44 claims concurrency safety while rasterise() is called outside the lock and mutates the shared opentype.Face/sfnt.Buffer. fbdev.Flip — the one function that converts pixels for real hardware, containing all the stride and channel-shift arithmetic — has no test, and canvas.go has no test file at all. Both are foundations for everything above them.
ordered_plan.files: internal/fbfont/font.go:44,149-157 (hold a sync.Mutex across rasterise; add a -race Glyph test); internal/fbdev/device_linux.go:191-219 (make mem/vinf/finf injectable; honour the Transp bitfield at 32bpp instead of writing byte(v>>24)); new internal/fbdev/canvas_test.go

ordered_plan.rationale: fbcon owns the console (CONFIG_FRAMEBUFFER_CONSOLE=y) and will repaint over anything drawn to /dev/fb0 — cursor blink, printk, echoed keystrokes. Today fbterm hides this; deleting fbterm removes the protection. Nothing in the tree does KDSETMODE (verified: zero hits for KDSETMODE|KD_GRAPHICS|vtcon across cmd/ internal/ panel/).
ordered_plan.files: new internal/fbvt/ (KDSETMODE KD_GRAPHICS on the panel VT, KD_TEXT restore on normal exit, panic and SIGTERM/SIGINT; optional /sys/class/vtconsole/vtcon*/bind unbind — CONFIG_VT_HW_CONSOLE_BINDING=y is enabled in the built kernel); os/buildroot/.../usr/bin/mcos-launch (keep the existing printk silencing)
ordered_plan.risk: Failing to restore KD_TEXT on a crash leaves the machine with a blank, unrecoverable console. Register the restore in a defer AND a signal handler AND a recover; test by killing the process with SIGKILL in QEMU and confirming the machine is still usable after the watchdog/respawn path.

ordered_plan.step: Write the evdev input package and bind it to the existing key handling
ordered_plan.rationale: The panel is keyboard-only and currently gets keys via Bubble Tea reading fbterm's stdin. Once the VT is in graphics mode there is no such stream. Nothing in the tree reads /dev/input (verified). This is a peer of the renderer, not an afterthought — a perfect first frame that accepts no input is the likeliest failure of this whole project.
ordered_plan.files: new internal/fbinput/ (read /dev/input/event*, decode EV_KEY, map to the key strings panel/app.go already switches on, including arrows, Enter, Esc, Shift+Tab, and Turkish layout characters); cmd/mcos-panel/main.go:55 (feed events into the tea.Program in place of stdin, or replace the tea loop entirely)
ordered_plan.risk: Keyboard layout and modifier handling are where this silently breaks (the OOBE needs to type Wi-Fi passwords and node names). Verify with a unit test that decodes recorded evdev frames into expected key strings, plus a manual QEMU pass typing a password containing Turkish characters.

ordered_plan.step: Bridge fbui to fbdev: the screen driver and render loop
ordered_plan.rationale: This is the single missing link between the finished widget layer and the hardware. fbui draws into an *image.RGBA; fbdev.Device.Flip pushes an *image.RGBA to /dev/fb0. Neither knows about the other.
ordered_plan.files: new internal/fbui/screen.go or cmd/mcos-panel (open /dev/fb0, size the canvas from the driver's actual xres/yres, fbfont.Load at a px size derived from screen height, fbui.NewUI, render, Flip); internal/fbui/theme.go:112 MetricsFor (make layout scale from the real cell size)
ordered_plan.risk: The mockups hardcode panel geometry (760x470, 880x560) at 1280x800. If layout does not scale, 1024x768 clips and 1920x1080 leaves a postage stamp. Verified by: golden-PNG tests that render every screen at 1024x768, 1280x800 and 1920x1080 and assert no widget crosses the canvas bounds.

ordered_plan.step: Port the panel screens from lipgloss strings to fbui Draw calls, screen by screen, with golden PNGs
ordered_plan.rationale: This is the bulk of request 1 and the largest single chunk of work (~7,000 non-test lines across panel/ and panel/theme/). Do NOT parse View()'s ANSI output — that would faithfully reproduce the character-cell look the user explicitly asked to remove. Keep the Bubble Tea model and state machine; replace only the rendering.
ordered_plan.files: panel/app.go:634 View() (becomes Draw), panel/view_dashboard.go, view_servers.go, view_detail.go, view_misc.go, components.go, panel/theme/tokens.go (the 13 codepoints the embedded font does not contain — ↻ ⌁ ▸ ◂ ◈ ◍ ★ ⚑ ⚙ ⚠ ✗ ✦ ℹ — become fbdraw/fbui shape calls); the strings.Repeat('─'/'█') sites at app.go:851, components.go:362-363,403, view_detail.go:674, view_misc.go:67-68, view_setup.go:712-713 become fbui.Divider / fbui.Progress
ordered_plan.risk: Largest scope, highest chance of stalling half-done. Mitigate by porting one screen per commit with a golden PNG test each, and by keeping the lipgloss path alive behind a flag until the last screen lands. The lipgloss surface to reproduce is small and already covered by fbui: RoundedBorder is the only border style used, there are 3 Place sites and 13 Join sites, and Align/MaxWidth/Margin/Italic/Underline are used nowhere.

ordered_plan.step: Drop fbterm from the launch path and decide what the GRUB recovery entry becomes
ordered_plan.rationale: fbterm is the layer being deleted; leaving it in place means the new renderer never actually runs on the appliance. The recovery entry (gfxpayload=text, nomodeset) has no /dev/fb0, so after the port it has no UI at all — that must be a decision, not an accident.
ordered_plan.files: os/buildroot/external/board/mcos/rootfs-overlay/usr/bin/mcos-launch (replace run_panel_fbterm with a direct framebuffer launch; keep a text fallback for serial and for the no-fb case); os/buildroot/external/board/mcos/rootfs-overlay/usr/bin/mcos-install:252-256 (either give recovery a framebuffer or relabel the menu entry honestly as a text/serial shell); os/buildroot/external/configs/mcos_defconfig (fbterm can be dropped once nothing uses it)
ordered_plan.risk: Removing fbterm removes the safety net that made a broken renderer merely ugly instead of fatal. Keep show_recovery() reachable and make the panel binary exit non-zero with a readable tty message when fbdev.Open fails, so a graphics failure degrades to a shell rather than a black screen.

ordered_plan.step: Build the display-settings screen: daemon-side grub.cfg rewrite plus the fbui screen
ordered_plan.rationale: Request 2's second half. The mockup already exists (internal/fbui/mockup_test.go TestMockupDisplaySettings, with a mode list). The privileged part is that nothing mounts the boot partition at runtime (fstab has no /boot entry; S99mcos mounts only MCOS-DATA), so the daemon must locate it, mount it, rewrite both configs, and unmount.
ordered_plan.files: new internal/daemon handler + internal/ipc method (display.modes / display.set); it must use /usr/bin/mcos-findfs MCOS-BOOT, mount, rewrite the gfxmode line in BOTH $ESP/boot/grub/grub.cfg and $ESP/EFI/BOOT/grub.cfg, sync, unmount; a new panel screen modelled on the existing mockup
ordered_plan.risk: Writing a bad grub.cfg bricks boot. Mitigate: never regenerate the file from scratch — rewrite only the 'set gfxmode=' line, always keep the trailing ',auto' fallback, write to a temp file on the same filesystem and rename, and verify the file parses and both menuentries survive before unmounting. Verified by: a script that runs the rewrite against a loopback disk image and diffs the result, plus a real reboot test. The Apply button must say a reboot is required — no runtime mode change is possible.

ordered_plan.step: Rewrite the OOBE install/selection screens on fbui and fix the logic defects
ordered_plan.rationale: Request 5. Doing this after the fbui port means writing each screen once instead of twice. The two must-fix defects are verified: Enter on the success screen re-runs mcos-install on the just-installed disk (panel/view_setup.go:411-416 has no installSuccess guard), and the install hard-reboots at step 5/10 so doSetupSave never runs and the installed system has no config.json despite mcos-install:305-325 assuming one.
ordered_plan.files: panel/view_setup.go — :411-416 (installSuccess guard that reboots; step reordering so config is saved before the install), :436-443 + :639 (Geri is a no-op on steps 2-5 while still being advertised), :192-197 (do not consume left/right/h/l/space when activeTextInput() != nil — the node-name field currently cannot accept h, l or space), :228 vs :873-880 (the Wi-Fi cursor can move onto rows the view never draws), :493-511 (seed buildConfig from the live config instead of DefaultConfig, which currently silently resets Turbo/AutostartServers/WAN/Features/Tier), :513-519 (a late javaSetupMsg clears s.loading mid-install), :1064-1072 (surface UpdateConfig and Persist failures — errMsg is routed to a.statusErr which View never renders while a.setup != nil); panel/app.go:151-156 (handle disksMsg.err instead of rendering an RPC failure as 'no disks found'); panel/messages.go:177-194 (dlPlugins is accepted and ignored; dlJava is honoured only on the install path and its errors are discarded)
ordered_plan.risk: Reordering the wizard steps touches the one flow that repartitions disks. Add panel unit tests (panel/view_setup_test.go already exists) that drive the state machine through both the install and the Atla path and assert exactly which commands are emitted. Add an explicit confirmation before doInstallOS — Enter is the universal continue key everywhere else, and back() from stepTheme lands on stepInstall with the cursor on the first disk.

ordered_plan.step: Add a generic local-artifact cache to the download helpers
ordered_plan.rationale: Foundation for request 3, and far better than special-casing Fabric. Every provider and every mod install funnels through exactly two functions, so one change makes all flavours bundleable and makes a second install of the same artifact work offline.
ordered_plan.files: internal/server/providers/provider.go:66 getJSON and :83 downloadTo (check a local artifact dir — e.g. /data/artifacts or /opt/mcos/artifacts — before the HTTP GET, and populate it after a successful GET); internal/catalog/catalog.go:178 DownloadTo (same)
ordered_plan.risk: Cache-key correctness. Key on the full URL (hashed) rather than the filename, or a 1.21.x server.jar will satisfy a request for a different version. Verified by a unit test with a stubbed HTTP transport that fails all requests and a pre-populated cache dir.

ordered_plan.step: Build the offline bundle and seed it into MCOS-DATA
ordered_plan.rationale: Request 3 proper. The seed mechanism already exists and is empty (mkusb.sh:207-213 mke2fs -d), costs zero initramfs bytes, and survives the permanent install via mcos-install:314's 'cp -a /data/.'.
ordered_plan.files: new scripts/mkbundle.sh (build-time, online: pin the exact MC version from the Fabric meta API; run the Fabric server launcher once in a scratch dir so .fabric/ and libraries/ are fully materialised; jlink a headless JRE 21 against the glibc toolchain; fetch the ViaFabric jar into mods/; emit .mcos-launch.json {jarFile:server.jar, launchArgs:[nogui], installed:true}, the matching server.json manifest, eula.txt, server.properties, and java/index.json with a model.JavaRuntime pointing at /data/java/temurin-21/bin/java); scripts/mkusb.sh:207-213 (populate $SEED from bundle/ before mke2fs -d); internal/daemon/handlers_net.go:88 (add the pinned version to fallbackVersions)
ordered_plan.risk: Three specific traps. (1) A jlink'd JRE built against a newer glibc will not start on this rootfs (BR2_TOOLCHAIN_BUILDROOT_GLIBC) — test bin/java inside the actual image, not on the build host. (2) If the bundled version is missing from fallbackVersions, the offline wizard cannot offer it and the bundle is unreachable. (3) The pure-ISO path (Makefile iso: ships only bzImage + initrd.img) has no data partition and therefore no bundle — document this, do not try to fix it by growing the 122 MB initramfs.

ordered_plan.step: Make the daemon actually find the bundled Java and install ViaFabric for mod loaders
ordered_plan.rationale: Without these two small changes the bundle sits on disk unused: handlers.go:400-413 decides Java presence purely from the index and then hard-errors on a failed Adoptium download, and compat.go:16 skips Via entirely for Fabric. detect.go:114 already lists /opt/mcos/java as a candidate but Detect() is only ever called from the java.detect RPC, which no panel view invokes.
ordered_plan.files: internal/daemon/daemon.go (call d.java.Detect() at startup); internal/server/compat.go:15-19 (add a SupportsMods branch installing viafabric into filepath.Join(dataDir, "mods"), mirroring contentDirFor in internal/daemon/handlers_catalog.go:31-40, and fix the misleading 'self-contained' comment at internal/server/providers/fabric.go:47-48); internal/daemon/handlers.go:400-413 and internal/server/manager.go:139-142 (say 'no network' plainly instead of surfacing a raw download error)
ordered_plan.risk: Calling Detect() at startup adds process spawns (java -version per candidate) to the boot path; bound it with a timeout and run it asynchronously so a hung binary cannot delay the daemon.

ordered_plan.step: End-to-end offline acceptance test in QEMU with no network
ordered_plan.rationale: This is the only verification that request 3 actually works, and it exercises the whole chain: seeded partition, Java index registration, IsInstalled short-circuit, mods/ contents, and server start. Every prior offline step is individually plausible and collectively easy to get wrong.
ordered_plan.files: new scripts/test-offline-boot.sh (boot the mkusb image in QEMU with -net none; assert the daemon registers the bundled JRE, that the create-server flow offers the pinned version, that the server reaches Running, and that the ViaFabric jar is present in mods/)
ordered_plan.risk: A pass here can still hide a first-run network fetch if QEMU is accidentally given a network device — assert '-net none' explicitly and grep the server log for connection attempts. Also re-run scripts/test-install-logic.sh and the full go test -race suite at this point, since the OOBE reordering and the UI port both touch code paths this test walks through.
